The interpolated temperature for FL 260 of about –26°C is 11°C warmer than standard. The best answer is 260° true; 43 kt.; ISA +10. (ISA is the International Standard Atmosphere. ISA temperature at sea level is 15°C and decreases at a rate of 2°/1,000 ft. up to 36,000 ft. MSL.) Answer (B) is incorrect. Forecast temperature is warmer, not colder, than ISA. Answer (C) is incorrect. Wind direction is degrees true, not magnetic.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 149 on page 817.) What will be the wind and temperature trend for a DEN-ICT-OKC flight at 11,000 feet?

choices.text: Wind shift from calm to a westerly direction.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. DEN-ICT-OKC 11,000 ft 값을 보간하면 바람은 DEN의 light and variable에서 ICT·OKC 약 2 kt로 약간 증가하는 추세이다.
questions.explanation_en: To determine the wind and temperature trend, the winds and temperatures aloft must be interpolated for 11,000 ft. The table below shows data for 9,000 and 12,000 ft. and the interpolated data for 11,000 ft. 9,000 12,000 11,000 DEN 9900+09 9900+04 9900+06 ICT 0607+08 9900+04 0602+05 OKC 1106+10 9900+05 1102+07 The best answer is that wind speed increases slightly from light and variable in DEN to 2 kt. at ICT and OKC. Answer (A) is incorrect. The temperature increases at OKC to a temperature higher than DEN. Answer (C) is incorrect. The wind shifts from calm to an easterly, not westerly, direction.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 149 on page 819.) What approximate wind direction, speed, and temperature (relative to ISA) are expected for a flight over OKC at FL 370?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. OKC FL340과 FL390을 보간하면 FL370은 약 260°/27 kt, -50°C이다. Tropopause 표준온도 약 -56°C와 비교하면 ISA +6°C이다.
questions.explanation_en: For conditions at FL 370 over OKC in Fig. 149, interpolate between values at FL 340 and FL 390. First decode the two given flight levels: FL 340 = 250° at 27 kt. and –43°C FL 390 = 270° at 27 kt. and –54°C Difference = 20° at 0 kt. and –11°C Interpolation for each value gives: FL 370 = 262° at 27 kt. and –50°C Since the FB is rounded to the nearest 10°, the wind direction is 260°. To compare the temperature to standard temperature, remember that the temperature in the tropopause (36,000 ft. MSL and above) is approximately –56°C. Thus, –50°C is ISA +6°C. (ISA is the International Standard Atmosphere. ISA temperature at sea level is 15°C and decreases at a rate of 2°/1,000 ft. up to 36,000 ft. MSL.) Answer (A) is incorrect. The direction is rounded to the nearest 10°, not 5°, and temperature is ISA +6°C, not +1°C. Answer (C) is incorrect. Winds are in degrees true, not magnetic, and temperature is ISA +6°C, not +10°C.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 149 on page 819.) What will be the wind and temperature trend for a DSM-LIT-SHV flight at 12,000 feet?

choices.text: Wind direction shift from northwest to southeast.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 12,000 ft에서 DSM-LIT-SHV 자료는 풍속이 22 kt→8 kt→6 kt로 감소하는 추세를 보인다.
questions.explanation_en: In determining the wind and temperature trend, it is easier to view in a table format. Note that, in this question, no interpolation is needed since 12,000 ft. is an altitude at which data are supplied from the Winds and Temperatures Aloft Forecast. Below is a table of the data: DSM LIT SHV 12,000 ft. 3022+00 2808+06 2106+06 During this flight, the wind speed decreases from 22 kt. to 8 kt. to 6 kt. Answer (B) is incorrect. The temperature increases, not decreases, en route. Answer (C) is incorrect. The wind direction shifts from northwest to southwest, not southeast.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 149 on page 819.) What will be the wind and temperature trend for an SAT ELP TUS flight at 16,000 feet?

choices.text: Wind direction shift from southwest to east.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 16,000 ft로 보간하면 SAT 약 200°/8 kt, ELP 약 030°/14 kt, TUS 약 080°/11 kt가 되어 항로를 따라 바람 방향이 남서풍 계열에서 동풍 계열로 크게 변한다.
questions.explanation_en: To determine the wind and temperature trend, the winds and temperatures aloft must be interpolated for 16,000 ft. The table below shows data for 12,000 and 18,000 ft. and the interpolated data for 16,000 ft. 12,000 18,000 16,000 SAT 1911+07 2006-07 2008-02 ELP 0615+08 0113-05 0314-01 TUS 0814+10 0810-05 0811+00 On this route, the wind direction shifts from southwest (200°) to east (080°). Answer (A) is incorrect. Temperatures increase, not decrease, slightly. Answer (B) is incorrect. Wind speed increases between SAT and ELP but decreases from ELP to TUS.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 149 on page 819.) What will be the wind and temperature trend for an STL-MEM-MSY flight at FL 330?

choices.text: Wind shift from west to north.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. FL330 보간자료에서 STL 약 56 kt, MEM 약 21 kt, MSY light and variable로 진행하므로 풍속이 점차 감소한다.
questions.explanation_en: To determine the wind and temperature trend, the winds and temperatures aloft must be interpolated for FL 330. The table below shows data for FL 300 and FL 340 and the interpolated data for FL 330. FL 300 FL 340 FL 330 STL 265435 265744 265642 MEM 261934 262144 262142 MSY 990034 990043 990041 During this flight, the wind speed decreases from 56 kt. to light and variable. Answer (B) is incorrect. The wind remains westerly in direction and becomes light and variable; it does not shift to the north. Answer (C) is incorrect. Temperature increases 1°C, not 5°C.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 149 below.) What is the forecasted wind direction, speed, and temperature over ABI at 30,000 feet?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ABI FL300 code 240833은 240°/8 kt, -33°C를 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: Find the winds aloft forecast for ABI on the top line of Fig. 149. Move to the right until you reach the column marked 30000, where it reads 240833. The 24 indicates a wind direction of 240°, 08 indicates a wind speed of 8 kt., and since all temperatures are negative above FL 240, the 33 indicates a –33°C temperature. Answer (A) is incorrect. For any forecasted wind speed between 100 kt. and 199 kt., the forecaster subtracts 100 from the speed and adds 50 to the direction. Thus, if the wind speed is 108 kt., the direction is coded as 74. Answer (C) is incorrect. Temperatures at altitudes above 24,000 ft. are negative. ratures Aloft Forecasts.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 145 on page 821.) What type of report is listed for Lubbock (KLBB) at 1818Z?

choices.text: An aviation selected special weather report.
A special report concerning very low station pressure.
A special METAR weather observation, concerning significant weather changes.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 1818Z에 발행된 KLBB의 SPECI는 정규관측 시각 사이에 SPECI 기준이 충족될 때 발행되는 특별 항공기상관측이다.
questions.explanation_en: At 1818Z (or 1818 UTC), KLBB issued a SPECI report, which is an aviation selected special weather report. The SPECI is a nonroutine aviation weather report taken when any of the SPECI criteria have been observed. Answer (B) is incorrect. Pressure changes do not require a SPECI. Any rapidly rising or falling pressure is reported in the remarks section. Answer (C) is incorrect. A SPECI is an aviation selected special weather report, not a special METAR. Also, a SPECI may be issued for other than weather changes, such as a volcanic eruption or a notification of an aircraft mishap.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 145 on page 821.) What was the local Central Standard Time of the Aviation Routine Weather Report at Austin (KAUS)?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. KAUS 131753Z는 13일 1753 UTC 발행을 뜻한다. CST는 UTC-6이므로 11:53 a.m. CST이다.
questions.explanation_en: The date/time after Austin (KAUS) on Fig. 145 is 131753Z. The first two digits are the date and the last four digits are the time, followed by Z to denote coordinated universal time (UTC). Thus, the report was issued at 1753 UTC. To determine Central Standard Time, you must subtract 6 hr. from UTC; thus, the time is 11:53 a.m. (1753 – 6 = 1153) CST. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is UTC adjusted to 24-hr. clock time (1753 = 5:53 p.m.). Answer (C) is incorrect. Central Standard Time is 6 hr. behind, not 5 hr. ahead of, UTC.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 145 on page 821.) What weather improvement was reported at Lubbock (KLBB) between 1750 and 1818 UTC?

choices.text: The wind shift and frontal passage at 1812Z.
The vertical visibility improved by 2,000 feet.
The temperature and dew point spread improved.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. KLBB의 vertical visibility는 1750Z VV010=1,000 ft에서 1818Z VV030=3,000 ft로 2,000 ft 개선되었다.
questions.explanation_en: The vertical visibility at KLBB at 1750 UTC was reported to be 1,000 ft. (VV010). At 1818 UTC, the vertical visibility was reported to be 3,000 ft. (VV030), an improvement of 2,000 ft. from the 1750 UTC report. Answer (A) is incorrect. While the wind did shift at 1812Z due to a frontal passage, wind is not a weather element. Answer (C) is incorrect. At 1750 UTC, the temperature was +3°C and the dew point was –01°C (03/M01), or a spread of 4°C. At 1818 UTC, both the temperature and dew point were –1°C (M01/M01), or a spread of 0°C. Thus, the temperature/dew point spread decreased, not increased or improved.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 145 on page 821.) What condition is reported at Dallas (KDAL)?

choices.text: The tops of the overcast is 10,000 feet.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. METAR altimeter setting은 A 뒤에 네 자리로 inHg를 표시한다. A3007은 30.07 inHg이다.
questions.explanation_en: Altimeter settings are reported in a four-digit format in inches of mercury prefixed with an “A” to denote the units of pressure. KDAL altimeter setting is coded as A3007, which means 30.07 inches of mercury. Answer (A) is incorrect. The base, not the top, of the overcast layer is 10,000 ft. Answer (B) is incorrect. The temperature/dew point spread is 8°C, not 8°F.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 145 on page 821.) What condition is reported at Childress (KCDS)?

choices.text: Heavy rain showers began 42 minutes after the hour.
The ceiling is solid overcast at an estimated 1,800 feet above sea level.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. KCDS METAR의 -SHRA는 light(-) shower(SH) rain(RA), 즉 약한 소나기성 비를 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: In the METAR for KCDS is the code –SHRA, which means there are light (–) showers (SH) and the precipitation type is rain (RA). Answer (B) is incorrect. Light, not heavy, rain showers began at 42 min. past the hour. Answer (C) is incorrect. Cloud height is expressed in AGL, not MSL. KCDS reports the bases of an overcast layer at 18,000 ft., not 1,800 ft., and METARs do not state whether the bases are estimated or measured.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 145 on page 821.) The peak wind at KAMA was reported to be from 320° true at 39 knots,

choices.text: with .43 of an inch liquid precipitation since the last report.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. PK WND 32039/43은 peak wind 320° true/39 kt가 해당 시각의 43분에 발생했다는 뜻이다. METAR가 1755Z이면 peak는 1743Z에 발생했다.
questions.explanation_en: Whenever the peak wind exceeds 25 kt., PK WND will be included in the remarks with three digits for direction and two or three digits for speed followed by the time (in hours and minutes or just minutes past the hour) of occurrence. The time of the METAR report for KAMA is 1755Z, and the remark PK WND 32039/43 means the peak wind 320° true at 39 kt. occurred at 43 min. past the hour, or at 1743Z. Answer (B) is incorrect. Gusts are not reported in a peak wind remark. Answer (C) is incorrect. The remark means that the peak wind occurred at 43 min. past the hour, not that .43 of an inch of precipitation has accumulated since the last report.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 145 below.) The minimums for the nonprecision approach at KAMA are 3/4 mile visibility and 400 feet. When operating under Part 121, can the pilot legally execute the approach with the given METAR data?

choices.text: Yes, they meet the minimum visibility requirements.
No, they do not meet the minimum visibility requirements.
No, they do not meet the minimum ceiling requirements. Figure 145. Aviation Routine

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. METAR visibility 3/4 SM이 접근 minimum과 같다면 Part 121에서는 ceiling과 관계없이 보고 visibility가 minimum 이상이므로 FAF를 지나 접근을 계속할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The visibility given in the METAR is 3/4 mile, equal to the minimum for the approach. Part 121 allows the approach to continue past the final approach fix if a weather report indicates the visibility is equal to or greater than the approach minimum, irrespective of the ceiling level. Answer (B) is incorrect. The visibility requirement of 3/4 mile is met. Answer (C) is incorrect. A minimum ceiling is not needed to begin an approach. Weather Reports (METAR).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: SPECI KGLS 131802Z 10012G21KT 060V140 2SM +SHRA SCT005 BKN035 OVC050CB 24/23 A2980 RMK RAB57 WS TKO RW09L WSHFT 58 FROPA. This SPECI report at Galveston (KGLS) indicates which condition?

choices.text: Wind steady at 100° magnetic at 12 knots, gusts to 21.
Precipitation started at 57 after the hour.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. KGLS SPECI RMK의 RAB57은 57분에 비 시작, WS TKO RW09L은 RWY 09L 이륙 중 wind shear, WSHFT 58 FROPA는 frontal passage로 58분에 wind shift가 발생했다는 뜻이다.
questions.explanation_en: The remarks (RMK) section of the SPECI report at KGLS indicates rain began at 57 min. past the hour (RAB57); wind shear occurred during takeoff on RWY 09L (WS TKO RW09L); and the wind shifted in direction at 58 min. past the hour due to a frontal passage (WSHFT 58 FROPA). Answer (A) is incorrect. The wind is variable, not steady, from 060° to 140° with the prevailing wind at 100°. Wind direction is referenced to true, not magnetic, north. Answer (C) is incorrect. The 5,000 ft. overcast layer is the base of cumulonimbus clouds (CB), not tower cumulus clouds (TCU).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: METAR KMAF 131756Z 02020KT 12SM BKN025 OVC250 27/18 A3009 RMK RAE44. Which weather condition is indicated by this METAR report at Midland (KMAF)?

choices.text: Rain of unknown intensity ended 16 minutes before the hour.
The ceiling was at 25,000 feet MSL.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. KMAF RMK의 RAE44는 해당 시각 44분에 비가 끝났다는 의미이다.
questions.explanation_en: The report at KMAF indicates RMK RAE44, which means remarks follow: rain ended 44 min. past the hour (or 16 min. before the hour). Answer (B) is incorrect. The ceiling is a broken layer at 2,500 ft. AGL (BKN025), not 25,000 ft. MSL. Answer (C) is incorrect. Wind direction is referenced to true, not magnetic, north.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: METAR KSPS 131757Z 09014KT 6SM -RA SCT025 OVC090 24/22 A3005. SPECI KSPS 131820Z 01025KT 3SM +RA FC OVC015 22/21 A3000. What change took place at Wichita Falls (KSPS) between 1757 and 1820 UTC?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. KSPS 1820Z SPECI의 FC는 funnel cloud가 관측되었다는 뜻이다.
questions.explanation_en: The special report (SPECI) for KSPS at 1820 UTC reports that a funnel cloud (FC) was observed. Answer (A) is incorrect. The rain intensity increased, not decreased, between 1757 and 1820 UTC. At 1757 UTC the rain was light (–RA), and at 1820 UTC the rain was heavy (+RA). Answer (B) is incorrect. The atmospheric pressure decreased, not increased. At 1757 UTC the altimeter setting was 30.05 in. of Hg (A3005), and at 1820 UTC the altimeter setting was 30.00 in. of Hg (A3000).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 146 on page 823.) What method was used to obtain the METAR at Tyler (KTYR) at 1753Z?

choices.text: Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS), having a precipitation discriminator.
Automatic Meteorological Observing Station (AMOS), with a precipitation discriminator.
Automated Weather Observing System (AWOS), without a precipitation discriminator.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. KTYR METAR의 AUTO는 완전 자동관측을 뜻하고, A02는 precipitation discriminator가 있는 automated station임을 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: After the date/time group on the METAR for KTYR is the contraction AUTO, which means that the METAR is a fully automated report. Currently, an ASOS is the only automated station that performs the basic observing functions necessary to generate a METAR report. Additionally, the remark A02 means the automated station has a precipitation discriminator. Answer (B) is incorrect. An AMOS is used at some sites, but it is not able to generate a METAR report. Currently, ASOS stations generate METAR reports. Answer (C) is incorrect. Currently, only the ASOS, not the AWOS, can perform the functions necessary to generate a METAR report. In the future, selected AWOS sites may be incorporated into the nationwide data collection network, and these stations will generate METAR reports. Additionally, a remark of A01, not A02, means that the automated station is without a precipitation discriminator.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 146 on page 823.) What was the ceiling at Walnut Ridge (KARG)?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Ceiling은 가장 낮은 BKN/OVC층 또는 vertical visibility이다. KARG의 OVC010은 1,000 ft AGL overcast ceiling을 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: The ceiling is the lowest broken or overcast layer (measured in hundreds of feet above ground level) or vertical visibility (measured in hundreds of feet) into an obscuration. The ceiling at KARG is reported to be overcast clouds at 1,000 ft. AGL (OVC010). Answer (B) is incorrect. The runway visual range for RWY 28 at KARG is 2,400 ft. (R28/2400 FT), not the ceiling. Answer (C) is incorrect. The ceiling is measured in hundreds of feet above ground level (AGL), not above mean sea level (MSL).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: METAR KHRO 131753Z 09007KT 7SM FEW020 BKN040CB 30/27 A3001. SPECI KHRO 131815Z 13017G26KT 3SM +TSRA SCT020 BKN045TCU 29/24 A2983 RMK RAB12 WS TKO LDG RW14R FRQ LTGICCG VC. What change has taken place between 1753 and 1815 UTC at Harrison (KHRO)?

choices.text: The ceiling lowered and cumulonimbus clouds developed.
Thundershowers began at 12 minutes past the hour.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. KHRO 1815Z SPECI의 +TSRA는 thunderstorm with heavy rain이고, RMK RAB12는 비가 12분에 시작되었음을 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: The special report (SPECI) taken at 1815 UTC at KHRO reports thunderstorm with heavy rain (+TSRA), and the remarks state that the rain began at 12 min. past the hour (RAB12). Answer (A) is incorrect. The ceiling (BKN) increased, not decreased, from 4,000 ft. to 4,500 ft., and towering cumulus clouds (TCU), not cumulonimbus clouds (CB), were reported at 1815 UTC. Answer (C) is incorrect. Visibility reduced to 3 SM, which is VFR, not IFR.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The prevailing visibility in the following METAR is METAR KFSM 131756Z AUTO 00000KT M1/4SM R25/0600V1000FT -RA FG VV004 06/05 A2989 RMK A02 $.
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 자동관측소에서 prevailing visibility가 1/4 SM 미만이면 M1/4SM으로 보고한다.
questions.explanation_en: Prevailing visibility is reported in statute miles with a space and then fractions of statute miles, as needed, with SM appended to it. This METAR was produced at an automated station, as indicated by the modifier AUTO. At an automated station, visibility of less than 1/4 SM is reported as M1/4SM. Answer (B) is incorrect. The letter M means that the visibility is less than 1/4 SM, not measured 1/4 SM. Answer (C) is incorrect. The letter M means that the visibility is less than 1/4 SM, not that the visibility is a mean (average) of 1/4 SM.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The VV001 in the following METAR indicates METAR KFSM 131756Z AUTO 00000KT M1/4SM R25/0600V1000FT -RA FG VV001 A2989 RMK AO2 VIS 3/4 RWY19 CHINO RWY19 $.

choices.text: an observer reported the vertical visibility as 100 feet.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. METAR의 VV001은 obscuration 속 vertical visibility 100 ft, 즉 indefinite ceiling 100 ft를 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: The sky condition in the METAR is shown as VV001, which means a vertical visibility (spoken as an indefinite ceiling) of 100 ft. Answer (A) is incorrect. The METAR was produced by a fully automated station without any human intervention, as indicated by the AUTO modifier. Thus, there is no observer. Answer (C) is incorrect. The vertical visibility, not variability value, is 100 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The symbol ($) at the end of the following METAR indicates that METAR KFSM 131756Z AUTO 00000KT M1/4SM R25/0600V1000FT -RA FG VV004 06/05 A2989 RMK A02 $.

choices.text: the latest information is transmitted over a discrete VHF frequency at KFSM.
the latest information is broadcast on the voice portion of a local NAVAID at KFSM.
maintenance is needed on the system.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 자동기상관측시스템이 정비 필요를 감지하면 METAR에 '$' maintenance indicator가 붙는다.
questions.explanation_en: A maintenance indicator (dollar) sign, $, is included when an automated weather reporting station detects that maintenance is needed on the system. Answer (A) is incorrect. The $ symbol indicates that maintenance is needed on the system, not that the latest information is transmitted over a discrete VHF frequency at KFSM. Answer (B) is incorrect. The $ symbol indicates that maintenance is needed on the system, not that the latest information is broadcast on the voice portion of a local NAVAID at KFSM.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A squall is a sudden increase of at least 16 knots in average wind speed to a sustained speed of

choices.text: 26 knots or more for at least 1 minute.
20 knots or more for at least 1 minute.
22 knots or more for at least 1 minute.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Squall은 평균풍속이 갑자기 최소 16 kt 증가해 22 kt 이상이 되고 그 상태가 최소 1분 지속되는 현상이며 METAR에서는 SQ로 보고한다.
questions.explanation_en: A squall is a sudden increase of at least 16 kt. in average wind speed to a sustained speed of 22 kt. or more for at least 1 minute. Squalls are reported in the METAR as weather phenomena by the code SQ. Answer (A) is incorrect. A squall is a sudden increase of at least 16 kt. in average wind speed to a sustained speed of 22 kt., not 26 kt., or more for at least 1 minute. Answer (B) is incorrect. A squall is a sudden increase of at least 16 kt. in average wind speed to a sustained speed of 22 kt., not 20 kt., or more for at least 1 minute.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: If squalls are reported at the destination airport, what wind conditions exist?

choices.text: Sudden increases in wind speed of at least 15 knots to a sustained wind speed of 20 knots, lasting for at least 1 minute.
Rapid variation in wind direction of at least 20° and changes in speed of at least 10 knots between peaks and lulls.
A sudden increase in wind speed of at least 16 knots, the speed rising to 22 knots or more for 1 minute or longer.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Squall의 기준은 풍속이 갑자기 최소 16 kt 증가하고 최종 풍속이 22 kt 이상이며 1분 이상 지속되는 것이다.
questions.explanation_en: A squall is a sudden increase in wind speed of at least 16 kt., the speed rising to 22 kt. or more, and lasting for at least 1 min. Answer (A) is incorrect. A squall is a sudden increase in wind speed of at least 16 kt., the speed rising to 22 kt. or more, and lasting for at least 1 min. Answer (B) is incorrect. A gust, not a squall, has a variation in wind speed of at least 10 kt. between peaks and lulls.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Data that may be added (manual weather augmentation) to the Automated Weather Observing System (AWOS) report is limited to

choices.text: the precipitation accumulation report, an automated variable visibility, and wind direction remark.
thunderstorms (intensity and direction), precipitation (type and intensity), and obstructions to visibility (dependent on the visibility being 3 miles or less).
density altitude, NOTAMs, and reported slant range visibility.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. AWOS METAR에 사람이 추가한 manual augmentation remark는 RMK에 들어간다. 일반적으로 thunderstorm의 강도·방향, 강수 종류·강도, 시정 3 SM 이하일 때의 obstruction to vision 등을 추가한다.
questions.explanation_en: Manual weather augmentation remarks added to an AWOS-generated METAR are located in the remarks section. As a general rule, the manual remarks are limited to thunderstorms (intensity and direction), precipitation (type and intensity), and obstructions to vision when the visibility is 3 SM or less. Answer (A) is incorrect. Wind direction is an automated feature, not manually added data, of the AWOS. Answer (C) is incorrect. Density altitude is an automated, not a manually inputted, remark.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: METAR KFSO 031053Z VRB02KT 7SM MIFG SKC 15/14 A3012 RMK SLP993 60000 T01500139 56012 In the above METAR, the SLP993 60000 indicates

choices.text: sea-level pressure 999.3 hectopascals which in the last 6 hours has dropped .4 hectopascals.
sea-level pressure 999.3 hectopascals and a trace amount of precipitation has occurred over the last 3 hours.
sea-level pressure 999.3 hectopascals and in the last 6 hours that four-tenths of an inch of precipitation has fallen.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. RMK SLP993은 sea-level pressure 999.3 hPa이다. 6xxxx group은 3/6시간 강수량을 inch의 십·일·0.1·0.01 단위로 표시하며 60000은 trace 강수를 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: In the remarks (RMK) section of the METAR, the coded group SLP993 means the sea-level pressure (SLP) is 999.3 hectopascals. A coded element beginning with the number 6 indicates the 3- and 6-hr. precipitation amount. The “6” is followed by four digits indicating precipitation about using tens, units, tenths, and hundredths of an inch. When a trace amount of precipitation has occurred, four zeros will follow the number 6 (60000). Answer (A) is incorrect. The coded group 60000 indicates an indeterminable amount of precipitation has occurred over the last 3 hr., not that the pressure has dropped 0.4 hectopascals over the last 6 hr. Answer (C) is incorrect. A coded group for four-tenths of an inch of precipitation over the last 6 hr. would be coded as 60040, not 60000. The four zeroes indicate an indeterminable amount of precipitation has occurred.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: METAR KFSO 031053Z VRB02KT 7SM MIFG SKC 15/14 A3012 RMK SLP993 SNINCR 1/10 In the above METAR, the SNINCR 1/10 indicates

choices.text: sea-level pressure 999.3 hectopascals and a snow depth of 10" and a 1" increase in the last hour.
sea-level pressure 999.3 hectopascals and 0.10" of snow on the runway landing zone during the last hour.
sea-level pressure 999.3 hectopascals and 1" of snow in the last 10 hours.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. SNINCR 표시는 지난 1시간 동안 적설이 1 inch 증가했고 현재 총 snow depth가 10 inches라는 뜻이다.
questions.explanation_en: SNINCR (Snow Increasing Rapidly) indicates a snow depth increase of 1 inch in the past hour with a total depth on the ground of 10 inches. Answer (B) is incorrect. SNINCR has to do with snow depth on the ground, not necessarily on the runway landing zone. Answer (C) is incorrect. SNINCR does not indicate the last 10 hours. It indicates the snow depth increase in the past hour and the total depth on the ground at the time of the METAR.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which primary source contains information regarding the expected weather at the destination airport at the ETA?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. TAF는 특정 기간, 보통 24시간 동안 공항에서 예상되는 기상상태를 간결하게 예보하며 ETA의 목적공항 예상기상을 판단하는 데 사용한다.
questions.explanation_en: A Terminal Aerodrome Forecast (TAF) is a concise statement of the expected meteorological conditions at an airport during a specified period (usually 24 hr.). Thus, a TAF contains information regarding the expected weather at the destination airport at the ETA. Answer (A) is incorrect. A low-level prog chart is a forecast of significant weather for the United States. It is not a forecast for a specific destination. Answer (B) is incorrect. A weather depiction chart is a national weather map of observed, not forecast, weather at a specific time. It is useful for flight planning but does not provide specific information about a particular destination.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Weather conditions expected to occur in the vicinity of the airport, but not at the airport, are denoted by the letters “VC.” When VC appears in a Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, it covers a geographical area of

choices.text: a 5-to-10 statute mile radius from the airport.
a 5-mile radius of the center of a runway complex.
10 miles of the station originating the forecast.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. TAF의 VC(vicinity)는 공항 자체가 아니라 공항에서 약 5~10 SM 범위 안에서 예상되는 현상을 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: When VC appears in a TAF, it applies to weather conditions expected to occur in an area within a 5- to 10-SM radius of the airport, but not at the airport itself. Answer (B) is incorrect. VC applies to weather conditions expected to occur in an area within a 5- to 10-SM radius from the airport, not within a 5-mile radius of the runway complex. Answer (C) is incorrect. VC applies to weather conditions expected to occur in the vicinity of the airport (within a 5- to 10-SM radius of the airport), not within 10 miles of the station originating the forecast.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What weather is predicted by the term VCTS in a Terminal Aerodrome Forecast?

choices.text: Thunderstorms are expected in the vicinity.
Thunderstorms may occur over the station and within 50 miles of the station.
Thunderstorms are expected between 5 and 25 miles of the runway complex.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. TAF의 VCTS는 thunderstorm이 공항 자체가 아니라 vicinity, 즉 약 5~10 SM 범위에서 예상된다는 뜻이다.
questions.explanation_en: The term VC (vicinity) applies to weather conditions expected within a 5- to 10-SM radius of the airport, but not at the airport itself. Thus, VCTS in a TAF means thunderstorms are expected in the vicinity of the airport. Answer (B) is incorrect. VC means within 5- to 10-SM from the airport, not 50 miles. Answer (C) is incorrect. A geographic area between 5 and 25 miles of the runway complex was the definition of the term vicinity in the old U.S. terminal forecast (FT), not the TAF.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which are the only cloud types forecast in the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. TAF에서 cumulonimbus가 예상되면 해당 cloud layer 뒤에 CB를 붙인다. TAF에서 별도로 예보하는 cloud type은 CB뿐이다.
questions.explanation_en: If cumulonimbus clouds are expected at the airport, the contraction CB is appended to the cloud layer that represents the base of the cumulonimbus cloud(s). Cumulo-nimbus clouds are the only cloud type forecast in the TAF. Answer (A) is incorrect. The only cloud type forecast in the TAF is cumulonimbus, not altocumulus. Answer (C) is incorrect. The only cloud type forecast in the TAF is cumulonimbus, not stratocumulus.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A calm wind that is forecast, in the International Terminal Aerodrome Forecast (TAF), is encoded as
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. TAF의 calm wind는 00000KT로 encode한다.
questions.explanation_en: In the International Terminal Aerodrome Forecast (TAF), a calm wind that is forecast is encoded as 00000KT. Answer (A) is incorrect. A variable wind is encoded as VRB when a forecast is for low wind speeds (3 kt. or less) followed by a wind speed, not two zeros. A calm wind will be encoded as 00000KT. Answer (C) is incorrect. A calm wind is encoded as 00000KT, not 00003KT.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 147 on page 827.) What type conditions can be expected for a flight scheduled to land at Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (KAUS) at 1200Z?

choices.text: Chance of 1 statute mile visibility and cumulonimbus clouds.
IFR conditions due to low visibility.
MVFR conditions due to low ceilings.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. KAUS 0900~1800Z 예보는 visibility >6 SM, BKN015 ceiling이므로 낮은 ceiling 때문에 MVFR이다. 비·mist에 의한 IFR 상황이 아니다.
questions.explanation_en: IFR conditions are due to low visibility in rain and mist, not low ceilings and fog. At KAUS from 0900 to 1800Z (UTC), the forecast is wind 150° at 10 kt., visibility greater than 6 SM, and a broken ceiling at 1,500 ft. AGL. Thus, the expected conditions are MVFR conditions due to a low ceiling that is below 3,000 ft. AGL. Answer (A) is incorrect. Visibility is forecast to be greater than 6 SM, not 1 SM. Answer (B) is incorrect. Visibility is forecast to be greater than 6 SM, not 1 SM.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: In the International Terminal Aerodrome Forecast (TAF), a variable wind direction is noted by “VRB” where the three digit direction usually appears. A calm wind appears in the TAF as
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. TAF에서 calm wind는 00000KT로 표시한다.
questions.explanation_en: In the International Terminal Aerodrome Forecast (TAF), a calm wind appears in the TAF as 00000KT. Answer (A) is incorrect. In the TAF, a calm wind appears in the TAF as 00000KT, not 00003KT. Answer (B) is incorrect. In the TAF, a calm wind appears in the TAF as 00000KT, not VRB00KT. For low wind speeds (3 kt. or less), VRB is used for wind direction.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A PROB40 (PROBability) HHhh group in an International Terminal Aerodrome Forecast (TAF) indicates the probability of
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. TAF의 PROB40 HHhh는 지정 시간대에 thunderstorm 또는 강수현상이 발생할 확률이 40%, 즉 30% 이상 50% 미만임을 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: A PROB40 (PROBability) HHhh group in a TAF indicates the probability of thunderstorms or other precipitation events. The PROB group is used when the occurrence of thunderstorms or precipitation is in the 30% to less than 50% range; thus, the probability value of 40 is appended to the PROB contraction. PROB40 is followed by a four-digit group giving the beginning time (HH) and ending time (hh) of the period during which thunderstorms or precipitation is expected. Answer (B) is incorrect. A PROB40 group in a TAF indicates the probability of thunderstorms or other precipitation events, not low visibility. Answer (C) is incorrect. A PROB40 group in a TAF indicates the probability of thunderstorms or other precipitation events, not high winds.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the single source reference that contains information regarding volcanic eruption, turbulence, and icing conditions for a specific region?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. In-flight aviation weather advisory는 특정 지역의 volcanic eruption, turbulence, icing 등의 정보를 제공한다.
questions.explanation_en: In-flight aviation weather advisories provide information on volcanic eruption, turbulence, and icing conditions for a specific region. Answer (A) is incorrect. The Ceiling and Visibility Analysis is prepared from METAR reports and gives only a broad overview of the observed condition at the valid time of the chart. It does not provide any information on volcanic eruption, turbulence, and icing conditions for a specific region. Answer (C) is incorrect. Low-Level Significant Weather Prog Charts provide freezing level information, but do not include specific information concerning icing conditions, turbulence, or volcanic eruptions.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What information is provided by a Convective Outlook (AC)?

choices.text: It describes areas of probable severe icing and severe or extreme turbulence during the next 24 hours.
It provides prospects of both general and severe thunderstorm activity and specific severe weather threats during the following 8 days.
It indicates areas of probable convective turbulence and the extent of instability in the upper atmosphere (above 500 mb).

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Convective Outlook은 향후 8일간의 일반 및 severe thunderstorm 가능성을 전망하며 high, moderate, enhanced, slight, marginal risk 구역 등을 표시한다.
questions.explanation_en: The convective outlook describes the prospects for general and severe thunderstorm activity during the following 8 days. Areas with a high, moderate, enhanced (ENH), marginal (MRGL), or slight risk of severe weather are included. Answer (A) is incorrect. Severe icing and severe or extreme turbulence are the subjects of SIGMETs. Answer (C) is incorrect. This information describes a 500-mb Constant Pressure Analysis Chart.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Maximum turbulence potential charts (GTG-3) are issued
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. GTG-3 maximum turbulence potential chart는 upper-level front와 jet stream 관련 CAT 가능성을 4차원으로 예측하는 computer-generated product이다. 매시간 갱신되며 6/9/12시간 forecast도 주기적으로 업데이트된다.
questions.explanation_en: Maximum turbulence potential charts (GTG-3) graphics are computer generated, four-dimensional forecasts of information related to the likelihood of encountering Clear Air Turbulence (CAT) associated with upper-level fronts and jet streams. This forecast is updated every hour and includes 06, 09, and 12-hour forecasts, which are updated every 3 hours, starting at 00Z. Answer (B) is incorrect. The maximum turbulence potential charts are updated hourly, not two times a day. Answer (C) is incorrect. This chart may come out every morning at 0400 hr., but it is updated hourly.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Isobars on a surface weather chart represent lines of equal pressure

choices.text: at a given atmospheric pressure altitude.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Surface analysis chart의 isobar는 sea-level pressure가 같은 지점을 연결하며 보통 4 mb(hPa) 간격이다. 이를 통해 표고가 다른 관측소의 기압을 비교할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Isobars on a surface analysis (weather) chart represent the sea level pressure pattern, usually spaced at 4-mb, or 4-hPa, intervals. This allows a comparison to be made of pressure reports by stations at various altitudes. Answer (A) is incorrect. The isobars are depicted at the sea level pressure pattern at 4-mb (4-hPa) intervals, not just at the surface. Answer (C) is incorrect. The isobars are reduced to sea level pressure, not any given atmospheric pressure altitude.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A prognostic chart depicts the conditions

choices.text: existing at the surface during the past 6 hours.
which presently exist from the 1,000-millibar through the 700-millibar level.
forecast to exist at a specific time in the future.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Prognostic chart는 차트의 valid time(UTC/Z)에 예상되는 기상상태를 나타내며 하루 네 차례 발행된다.
questions.explanation_en: Prognostic charts show conditions as they are forecast to be at the valid time (UTC or Zulu) for the chart. The charts are issued four times daily. Answer (A) is incorrect. Prognostic charts relate to the future, not the past. Answer (B) is incorrect. Low-level prognostic charts are issued for the surface and 24,000 ft., which is 400 mb. One thousand mb is very close to the surface; i.e., sea level is 1,013 mb. Seven hundred mb is approximately 10,000 ft. MSL.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: For international flights, a U.S. High-Level Significant Weather Prognostic Chart is prepared for use

choices.text: between 25,000 feet and 63,000 feet pressure altitude.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. High-Level SIGWX Prognostic Chart는 국제비행을 위해 AWC가 작성하며 대략 FL250~FL630(25,000~63,000 ft pressure altitude) 구간을 다룬다.
questions.explanation_en: Numerous High-Level Significant Weather Prognostic Charts are produced by the Aviation Weather Center (AWC) for international flights. They are prepared for flights between 25,000 ft. and 63,000 ft. pressure altitude (or FL 250 to FL 630). Answer (A) is incorrect. High-level prognostics for international flight are prepared for FL 250 to FL 630, not any altitude above 29,000. Answer (C) is incorrect. The base of the International High-Level Prognostic is FL 250, not FL 180.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Forecast winds and temperatures aloft for an international flight may be obtained by consulting

choices.text: low-level significant weather prog charts published by the departure location host country.
the current Ceiling and Visibility Analysis appropriate to the route.
Wind and Temperature Aloft Charts prepared by the U.S. National Centers for Environmental Prediction (NCEP).

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 국제비행의 forecast winds and temperatures aloft는 NCEP가 작성하는 Winds and Temperatures Aloft Chart에서 얻을 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Forecast winds and temperatures aloft for an international flight may be obtained by consulting Winds and Temperatures Aloft Charts prepared by the U.S. National Centers for Environmental Prediction (NCEP). Answer (A) is incorrect. Low-level significant weather prog charts are forecasts of general weather conditions and do not contain forecasts of the winds and temperatures aloft. Answer (B) is incorrect. The Ceiling and Visibility Analysis indicates current weather and does not forecast winds and temperatures aloft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What sources reflect the most accurate information on current and forecast icing conditions?

choices.text: Low-Level Sig Weather Prog Chart, RADAT’s, and the Area Forecast.
PIREP’s, Area Forecast, and the Freezing Level Chart.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 특정 지역의 현재 icing 상태는 PIREP이 가장 직접적이며 type과 intensity를 포함할 수 있다. AIRMET Zulu는 icing/freezing level, SIGMET은 severe icing에 발행된다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilot reports (PIREPs) can reflect the most current icing conditions for a specific area, including type and intensity. AIRMET Zulu is for icing and freezing levels for a specified time and normally an outlook. A SIGMET is issued for areas of severe icing. Answer (A) is incorrect. Low-level sig weather prog charts do not forecast icing conditions but do forecast freezing levels, and an area forecast does not provide any information on icing conditions. Answer (B) is incorrect. A freezing level chart cannot be used to determine current or forecast icing conditions, and an area forecast does not provide any information on icing conditions.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A public severe thunderstorm watch implies

choices.text: 58 mph winds or greater and/or surface hail of 1 inch or more in diameter.
45 mph winds or greater and/or surface hail of 1 inch or more in diameter.
50 knots or greater and/or surface hail of 1/2 inch or greater.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. NWS severe thunderstorm watch는 58 mph(50 kt) 이상 지상풍 및/또는 직경 1 inch 이상 지상 hail 가능 조건에서 발행될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The National Weather Service may issue a public severe thunderstorm watch when conditions are favorable to winds of 58 mph (50 kt.) or greater and/or surface hail of 1 inch or more in diameter. Answer (B) is incorrect. The threshold for winds that would trigger a severe thunderstorm watch is 58 mph, not 45 mph. Answer (C) is incorrect. Both the wind and hail values for a severe thunderstorm watch exceed those provided by this answer option. The correct values are 58 mph or greater and a 1-inch diameter or larger.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 153 below.) What type weather system is approaching the Oregon Coast from the northwest?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Constant pressure chart의 height contour 변화를 보면 3차원 기압계를 파악할 수 있다. Oregon coast로 접근하는 contour height가 내륙보다 낮다면 저기압이 접근하는 것이다.
questions.explanation_en: A three-dimensional picture can be developed by following the change in height of the height contours. These are the solid lines on Fig. 153, and the height is indicated on the lines. The contour that is approaching the Oregon coast is lower than the contours over the northwestern U.S. Thus, a low-pressure area must be approaching. Answer (B) is incorrect. The height contours would increase, not decrease, for a high. Answer (C) is incorrect. Pressure systems, not fronts, are depicted on a constant pressure chart.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 153 below, Figure 154 on page 831, and Figure 155 on page 831.) What is the relative moisture content of the air mass along the California coast?

choices.text: Dry in the southern part of the state, with increased chance for wet conditions in the mid portion, then drying over the northern section.
Moist enough for condensation along the length of the coast.
Very wet with high potential for condensation.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. California coast의 200/300/500 mb temperature-dew point spread를 비교하면 500·200 mb는 비교적 건조하고 300 mb에서 northern California의 수분이 더 많다.
questions.explanation_en: Determine the moisture content by comparing the temperature/dew point spread of the stations along the California coast at the 200-, 300-, and 500-mb pressure levels. The spread, if given, is located at the lower left of the station symbol. Both the 500- and 200-mb charts indicate relatively wide spread dry conditions. The 300-mb chart shows that moisture is high in northern California. Answer (B) is incorrect. There is very little moisture, as depicted by the wide temperature/dew point spread. Answer (C) is incorrect. The air mass is dry, not wet (note wide temperature/ dew point spreads).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 153 below, Figure 154 on page 831, and Figure 155 on page 831.) Interpret the path of the jetstream.

choices.text: Northern California coast, over Utah, turns southerly to the Gulf of Mexico, turning northeast over Florida.
Oregon, Idaho, Wyoming, Nebraska, Iowa, and across the Great Lakes.
The Alaska area, across Canada to Montana, South Dakota, then across the Great Lakes area. Figure 153. 500 MB Analysis He

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Jet stream 경로는 300/200 mb chart의 isotach를 비교해 찾는다. 50 kt 이상 바람대가 central California coast→Utah→Gulf→Florida→북동쪽으로 이어진다.
questions.explanation_en: To interpret the path of the jet stream, compare the isotachs on the 300- and 200-mb charts. The jet stream has winds of 50 kt. or greater. These greater wind speeds are found from the central California coast to Utah, then southward to the Gulf, returning across Florida and then northeastward. Answer (B) is incorrect. The isotachs over the Great Lakes are between 30 and 50 kt. Answer (C) is incorrect. The isotachs over the central U.S. are between 20 and 40 kt. ights/Temperature Chart.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 153 below, Figure 154 on page 833, and Figure 155 on page 833.) What is the approximate temperature for a flight from southern California to central Kansas at FL 350?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. FL350 온도는 300 mb와 200 mb 자료를 보간한다. 항로상의 평균 기온변화를 적용하면 약 -44°C로 추정된다.
questions.explanation_en: You will need to use the 300-mb (FL 390) chart and the 200-mb (FL 300) chart and interpolate for FL 350. The temperature is located in the upper left corner of the station on a constant pressure chart. On the 300-mb chart, the station in Southern California is reporting –36°C. Following the reporting stations along the intended flight path, you will find temperatures of –36, –38, –39, –42, and –41°C on the 300-mb chart. Similarly, you will find temperatures of –47, –47, –48, –48, and –52°C on the 200-mb chart. When averaging these temperatures at each level, the difference is about 9°, or approximately 1° per thousand feet of altitude. For FL 350, the estimated temperature would be –44°C. Answer (A) is incorrect. The approximate average temperature at FL 390 is –48°C. Answer (B) is incorrect. The approximate temperature at FL 300 is –39°C.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 153 below, Figure 154 on page 833, and Figure 155 on page 833.) Determine the approximate wind direction and velocity at FL 240 over the station in central Oklahoma.

choices.text: 100° at 30 knots. Figure 153. 500 MB Analysis He

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. FL180에서 280°/25 kt, FL300에서 280°/35 kt라면 FL240 보간값은 약 280°/30 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: To determine the approximate wind direction, you must interpolate between values for FL 180 (500-mb chart) and FL 300 (300-mb chart). The wind direction and speed are determined by the flag at the reporting station. First decode the two given pressure levels: FL 180 (500 mb) = 280° at 25 kt. FL 300 (300 mb) = 280° at 35 kt. Difference = 0° at 10 kt. Interpolation for each value gives the following: FL 240 = 280° at 30 kt. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is the wind direction and speed at the 500-mb pressure level (FL 180). Answer (C) is incorrect. This is found by misreading the wind direction symbol. ights/Temperature Chart.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Constant Pressure Analysis Charts contain contours, isotherms, and some contain isotachs. The contours depict

choices.text: ridges, lows, troughs, and highs aloft.
highs, lows, troughs, and ridges on the surface.
highs, lows, troughs, and ridges corrected to MSL.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Constant pressure analysis chart에는 contour와 isotherm, 일부에는 isotach가 있다. Contour는 같은 geopotential height를 연결하며 상층의 high/low/trough/ridge를 지상 isobar처럼 나타낸다.
questions.explanation_en: Constant pressure analysis charts contain contours and isotherms, and some contain isotachs. Contours are lines of equal height and depict highs, lows, troughs, and ridges aloft in the same manner as isobars on the surface chart. Answer (B) is incorrect. Contours depict highs, lows, troughs, and ridges aloft, not on the surface. Answer (C) is incorrect. Contour heights are expressed as pressure altitudes in a standard atmosphere, not corrected to MSL.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Vertical wind shear can be determined by comparing winds on vertically adjacent constant pressure charts. The vertical wind shear that is critical for probability of turbulence is
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Probable turbulence에 중요한 vertical wind shear 기준은 1,000 ft당 약 5 kt 이상이다.
questions.explanation_en: The vertical wind shear critical for probable turbulence is 5 kt. or more per 1,000 ft. Answer (A) is incorrect. The vertical wind shear critical for probable turbulence is 5 kt. or more per 1,000 ft., not 4 kt. or more per 1,000 ft. Answer (C) is incorrect. The vertical wind shear critical for probable turbulence is 5 kt. or more per 1,000 ft., not greater than 8 kt. per 1,000 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The horizontal wind shear, critical for turbulence (moderate or greater) per 150 miles is

choices.text: not a factor, only vertical shear is a factor.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Moderate 이상 turbulence와 관련된 중요한 horizontal wind shear는 150 NM당 18 kt 초과이다.
questions.explanation_en: The horizontal wind shear critical for turbu-lence (moderate or greater) is greater than 18 kt. per 150 NM. Answer (A) is incorrect. The horizontal wind shear critical for turbulence is greater than 18 kt., not 18 kt. or less. Answer (C) is incorrect. Both horizontal and vertical wind shears are critical for turbulence.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: If a SIGMET alert is announced, how can information contained in the SIGMET be obtained?

choices.text: ATC will announce the hazard and advise when information will be provided in the FSS broadcast.
By contacting a weather watch station.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 기상 advisory alert를 들었지만 내용을 받지 못했거나 자기 비행에 해당하는지 불확실하면 가장 가까운 FSS에 연락해 관련 여부를 확인해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots, upon hearing the alert notice, if they have not received the advisory or are in doubt, should contact the nearest FSS and ascertain whether the advisory is pertinent to their flights. Answer (A) is incorrect. ATC does not advise when to listen to an FSS broadcast; rather, they tell you to contact FSS. Answer (B) is incorrect. The pilot may monitor an FSS broadcast or contact any FSS. A weather watch station is a nonsense term.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which type weather conditions are covered in the Convective SIGMET?

choices.text: Embedded thunderstorms, lines of thunderstorms, and thunderstorms with 3/4-inch hail or tornadoes.
Cumulonimbus clouds with tops above the tropopause and thunderstorms with 1/2-inch hail or funnel clouds.
Any thunderstorm with a severity level of VIP 2 or more.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Convective SIGMET은 severe thunderstorm(풍속 >50 kt, hail ≥3/4 inch, tornado), embedded thunderstorm, line of thunderstorms, 또는 일정 면적의 강한 thunderstorm 활동 등에 발행된다.
questions.explanation_en: Convective SIGMETs are issued for (1) severe thunderstorm due to surface winds greater than 50 kt., hail at the surface equal to or greater than 3/4 in. in diameter, or tornadoes; (2) embedded thunderstorms; (3) line of thunderstorms; or (4) thunderstorms greater than or equal to VIP level 4 affecting 40% or more of an area at least 3,000 square mi. Answer (B) is incorrect. Cumulonimbus clouds with tops above the tropopause is not a weather condition covered in a convective SIGMET. Answer (C) is incorrect. Thunderstorms must be at least VIP level 4, not level 2.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 148 below.) Which system in the Convective SIGMET listing has the potential of producing the most severe storm?

choices.text: The storms in Texas and Oklahoma.
The storms in Colorado, Kansas, and Oklahoma.
The isolated storm 50 miles northeast of Memphis (MEM).

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. MEM 북동쪽 50 mi의 isolated thunderstorm은 VIP level 5(intense)이고 top이 45,000 ft 이상이어서 매우 큰 수직발달을 보인다.
questions.explanation_en: The isolated thunderstorm 50 mi. northeast of MEM is a VIP level 5 (intense) storm. With a top above 45,000 ft., extensive vertical development is taking place. Answer (A) is incorrect. The storms in Texas and Oklahoma do not have such extensive development (tops 30,000 ft.) as the storm NE of Memphis (MEM). Answer (B) is incorrect. The storms in Colorado, Kansas, and Oklahoma do not have such extensive vertical development (tops of 38,000 ft.) as the storm NE of Memphis (MEM).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 148 below.) What time period is covered by the outlook section of the Convective SIGMET?

choices.text: 2 to 6 hours after the valid time.
No more than 2 hours after the valid time. Figure 148. Conv

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Convective SIGMET outlook은 valid time 이후 약 2~6시간 동안 추가 Convective SIGMET이 필요할 가능성이 있는 thunderstorm system의 forecast와 meteorological discussion이다.
questions.explanation_en: The outlook for a particular region is appended to the convective SIGMET. The outlook is a forecast and meteorological discussion for thunderstorm systems that are expected to require convective SIGMET issuances during a period 2 to 6 hr. after the valid time. Note that on Fig. 148 the outlook is good until 2355Z, which is 4 hr. after the valid time of 1955Z. Answer (A) is incorrect. The outlook is for a period of 2 to 6 hr., not 24 hr., after the valid time. Answer (C) is incorrect. The outlook can cover up to 6 hr. after the valid time. ective SIGMET.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A severe thunderstorm is one in which the surface wind is

choices.text: 58 mph or greater and/or surface hail is 3/4 inch or more in diameter.
50 knots or greater and/or surface hail is 1/2 inch or more in diameter.
45 knots or greater and/or surface hail is 1 inch or more in diameter.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Severe thunderstorm 기준은 지상풍 ≥58 mph(50 kt), 지상 hail 직경 ≥3/4 inch, 또는 tornado 발생이다.
questions.explanation_en: A severe thunderstorm is one in which the surface winds are greater than or equal to 58 mph (50 kt.), hail at the surface is greater than or equal to 3/4 in. in diameter, or tornadoes are present. Answer (B) is incorrect. A severe thunderstorm is one in which the surface winds are 50 kt. or greater or hail at the surface is 3/4 in., not 1/2 in., or more in diameter. Answer (C) is incorrect. A severe thunderstorm is one in which the surface winds are 50 kt., not 45 kt., or greater or hail at the surface is 3/4 in., not 1 in., or more in diameter.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When you hear a SIGMET on an ATC frequency forecasting severe icing conditions on the route to your destination, you plan for

choices.text: the installed transport category airplane ice protection system protecting against all types and levels of icing as designed.
very little airframe icing because of an OAT of -10°C or colder, the moisture is already frozen and cannot adhere to airplane surfaces.
the possibility of freezing rain and freezing drizzle that can accumulate on and beyond the limits of any system.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Severe icing은 얼음 축적률이 너무 커 deicing/anti-icing 장비로도 위험을 줄이거나 통제하지 못하는 상태이다.
questions.explanation_en: Severe icing is defined by the rate of accumulation such that deicing/anti-icing equipment fails to reduce or control the hazard. Answer (A) is incorrect. The issuance of a severe icing SIGMET implies that ALL aircraft and their related deicing/ anti-icing equipment may not be sufficient to control the icing hazard. Answer (B) is incorrect. A SIGMET is an issued weather advisory. It locates an area of weather significant to the safety of all aircraft. If a SIGMET is issued that forecasts icing, plan for severe icing rather than very little airframe icing.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: SIGMETs may be issued for the contiguous U.S.

choices.text: and as convective SIGMETs for Alaska and Hawaii when squall lines are forecast.
and as convective SIGMETs for Alaska when obscured thunderstorms are forecast.
as convective SIGMETs when obscured thunderstorms are forecast.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. CONUS에서는 thunderstorm에 일반 SIGMET 대신 Convective SIGMET을 사용한다. Convective SIGMET은 severe 이상 turbulence, severe icing, low-level wind shear 가능성을 내포한다.
questions.explanation_en: Convective SIGMETs are issued for the conterminous U.S. (CONUS) instead of SIGMETs for thunderstorms. Any Convective SIGMET implies severe or greater turbulence, severe icing, and low-level wind shear. This includes the 48 states within the contiguous U.S. Answer (A) is incorrect. Conterminous and contiguous U.S. does not include Alaska and Hawaii. Answer (B) is incorrect. Obscured thunderstorms are covered by normal SIGMETs in Alaska, not convective SIGMETs.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Convective SIGMETs are issued for a line of thunderstorms at least

choices.text: 100 miles long with severe thunderstorms affecting 50 percent of its length.
40 miles long with thunderstorms affecting 50 percent of its length.
60 miles long with thunderstorms affecting 40 percent of its length.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Convective SIGMET은 thunderstorm line이 최소 60 mi 길이이고 40% 이상에서 뇌우가 있거나, 최소 3,000 sq mi 영역의 40% 이상이 매우 강한 radar/satellite/lightning signature를 보이는 active thunderstorm일 때 발행될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: A convective SIGMET will be issued when (1) a line of thunderstorms is at least 60 miles long with thunderstorms affecting at least 40% of its length or (2) an area of active thunderstorms is (a) affecting at least 3,000 square miles, (b) covering at least 40% of the area concerned, and (c) exhibiting a very strong radar reflectivity intensity or a significant satellite or lightning signature. Answer (A) is incorrect. A convective SIGMET will be issued when a line of thunderstorms is at least 60 miles long, not 100 miles long. Answer (B) is incorrect. A convective SIGMET will be issued when a line of thunderstorms is at least 60 miles long, not 40 miles long.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Convective SIGMETs are issued for severe thunderstorms

choices.text: occurring for more than one hour of the valid period.
occurring for more than 30 minutes of the valid period.
affecting more than 1,000 square miles of airspace.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Embedded 또는 severe thunderstorm이 valid period 중 30분 넘게 지속될 것으로 예상되면 영역 크기와 관계없이 Convective SIGMET을 발행한다.
questions.explanation_en: Convective SIGMETs are issued for embedded or severe thunderstorms expected to occur for more than 30 minutes during the valid period regardless of the size of the area. Answer (A) is incorrect. The time specified is for more than 30 minutes during the valid period. Answer (C) is incorrect. Convective SIGMETs are issued for an area of active thunderstorms affecting at least 3,000 square miles, not 1,000 square miles.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A SIGMET is issued when weather affects
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. SIGMET은 예보관 판단상 항공운항 안전에 중대한 영향을 주는 현상이 최소 약 3,000 sq mi 지역에 영향을 주거나 줄 것으로 예상될 때 발행될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: A SIGMET may be issued in the contiguous U.S. when certain conditions are affecting or, in the judgment of the forecaster, are expected to affect an area of at least 3,000 square miles of an area judged to have a significant impact on the safety of aircraft operations. Answer (A) is incorrect. The correct answer is 3,000 square miles, not 1,000 square miles. Answer (C) is incorrect. A SIGMET may be issued in the contiguous U.S. when certain conditions are affecting or, in the judgment of the forecaster, are expected to affect an area of at least 3,000 square miles of an area, not 5,000 square miles or more.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: SIGMETs (other than domestic convective SIGMETs) may be valid for not more than

choices.text: 4 hours for other phenomena and may be issued 2 hours before the valid time.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. SIGMET 유효기간은 hurricane 관련 현상은 6시간, 기타 현상은 4시간이며 현상이 계속되면 업데이트해 재발행한다.
questions.explanation_en: SIGMETs are issued for 6 hour periods for conditions associated with hurricanes and 4 hours for all other events. If conditions persist beyond the forecast period, the SIGMET is updated and reissued. Answer (A) is incorrect. An unscheduled SIGMET that is issued is valid at the time it is issued, not 2 hours before the valid time. Answer (C) is incorrect. SIGMETs may be valid for not more than 4 hours, not 6 hours.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A SIGMET may be issued

choices.text: for an area where conditions are deemed to have a significant effect on the safety of aircraft operations.
when expectations for dust storms or icing is predicted to be higher than 40% over a 1,000 square mile area.
for an area where conditions are likely to develop air turbulence above FL 310.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. SIGMET은 지정된 위험현상이 발생했거나 발생할 것으로 예상되어 항공운항 안전에 중대한 영향을 준다고 판단될 때 발행한다.
questions.explanation_en: A SIGMET may be issued when any of the specific conditions occur or are expected to occur in an area deemed to have a significant effect on the safety of aircraft operations. Answer (B) is incorrect. Two of the specific conditions for issuing a SIGMET are for severe icing not associated with thunderstorms and dust storms reducing visibility to 3 miles of less. However, there is no percentage or area requirement associated with this specific condition. Answer (C) is incorrect. SIGMETs are for hazardous weather to all aircraft, not necessarily about where conditions are likely to develop air turbulence above FL 310.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The Mid-Level Significant weather (SIGWX) Chart is used to determine an overview of flying weather conditions between what altitudes?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Mid-Level SIGWX Chart는 10,000 ft MSL~FL450 범위의 주요 비행기상을 한눈에 보여주며 출발 전·비행 중 flight planning과 weather briefing에 사용할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Dispatchers and flight crew members can use the Mid-Level Significant Weather (SIGWX) Chart to determine an overview of selected flying weather conditions. The altitude areas for this chart are between 10,000 feet MSL and FL 450. This information can be used for flight planning and weather briefings before departure and during flight. Answer (A) is incorrect. The SIGWX Chart altitudes are in Mean Sea Level (MSL) and not Above Ground Level (AGL). FL 450 is not referred to as 45,000 feet. It is referred to as Flight Level (FL) at a specific barometric pressure. Answer (B) is incorrect. The altitude areas for the SIGWX Chart are in Mean Sea Level (MSL) and not Above Ground Level (AGL).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The Federal Aviation Administration’s Flight Information Service Data Link (FISDL) is designed to provide data on a common frequency to flight crews from

choices.text: 17,500 feet AGL down to 5,000 feet MSL.
17,500 feet MSL down to 5,000 feet AGL.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. FISDL은 산악지형 때문에 불가능한 곳을 제외하고 continental U.S.에서 약 5,000 ft AGL~17,500 ft MSL 범위 커버리지를 목표로 설계되었다.
questions.explanation_en: The FAA’s Flight Information Service Data Link (FISDL) system is designed to provide coverage throughout the continental U.S. from 5,000 ft. AGL to 17,500 ft. MSL, except in those areas where this is unfeasible due to mountainous terrain. Answer (A) is incorrect. The FAA’s FISDL system is designed to provide coverage from 5,000 ft. AGL to 17,500 ft. MSL, not 5,000 ft. MSL to 17,500 ft. AGL. Answer (C) is incorrect. The FAA’s FISDL system is designed to provide coverage from 5,000 ft. AGL, not 5,000 ft. MSL, to 17,500 ft. MSL.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The Federal Aviation Administration’s Flight Information Service Data Link (FISDL) provides what products?

choices.text: Convective SIGMETs, PIREPs, AWWs, and NOTAMs.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. FISDL은 METAR, SPECI, TAF/수정본, SIGMET, Convective SIGMET, AIRMET, urgent/routine PIREP, AWW 등을 무료로 제공한다.
questions.explanation_en: The FAA’s Flight Information Service Data Link (FISDL) provides, free of charge, METARs, SPECIs, TAFs (and their amendments), SIGMETs, convective SIGMETs, AIRMETs, PIREPs (both urgent and routine), and AWWs (issued by the FAA or NWS). Answer (B) is incorrect. While the FAA’s FISDL does provide SPECIs, SIGMETs, and AIRMETs, it does not provide NOTAM information. Answer (C) is incorrect. While the FAA’s FISDL does provide convective SIGMETs, PIREPs, and AWWs, it does not provide any information about NOTAMs.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The Federal Aviation Administration’s Flight Information Service Data Link (FISDL) products, such as ground radar precipitation maps,

choices.text: may be used instead of the aircraft radar.
are not appropriate for finding a path through a weather hazard area.
may be used to find a path through a weather hazard area.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. FISDL의 radar precipitation map 같은 제품은 severe weather 사이를 전술적으로 통과하는 tactical avoidance 용도가 아니다. 위험구역 전체를 피하도록 항로를 선택하는 strategic decision에 사용해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: FISDL products, such as ground-based radar precipitation maps, are not appropriate for use in tactical severe weather avoidance, such as negotiating a path through a weather hazard area. FISDL supports strategic weather decision making, such as route selection to avoid a weather hazard area in its entirety. Answer (A) is incorrect. FISDL products, such as ground-based radar precipitation maps, are not appropriate for use in tactical severe weather avoidance. Airborne weather radar is appropriate for this purpose under certain conditions. Answer (C) is incorrect. FISDL products, such as ground-based radar precipitation maps, are not appropriate for use in tactical severe weather avoidance, such as negotiating a path through a weather hazard area.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim

subunit.title: Terminal Weather Information for Pilot System (TWIP)

questions.question: What weather database can a dispatcher access concerning wind shear activity at an airport?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Dispatcher는 TWIP database를 이용해 공항에서 wind shear 활동이 시작되거나 끝날 때 특정 항공기에 메시지를 보낼 수 있다.
tags: Terminal Weather Information for Pilot System (TWIP)
questions.explanation_en: Dispatchers can access the TWIP database and send messages to specific aircraft whenever wind shear activity begins or ends at an airport. Answer (B) is incorrect. AWOS is an automated weather observation station used by pilots at uncontrolled airports or airports with low traffic volume. It is a recording, not a database. Answer (C) is incorrect. ATIS is an automatic terminal information service used by pilots entering controlled airspace. It is a recording, not a database.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is an important characteristic of wind shear?

choices.text: It is primarily associated with the lateral vortices generated by thunderstorms.
It usually exists only in the vicinity of thunderstorms, but may be found near a strong temperature inversion.
It may be associated with either a wind shift or a windspeed gradient at any level in the atmosphere.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Wind shear는 바람속도 벡터가 변하는 비율이며 풍속, 풍향 또는 둘 다의 변화일 수 있다. 대기의 어느 고도에서도 wind shift나 wind-speed gradient 형태로 발생할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Wind shear is the rate of change of wind velocity. The differences may be in wind speed, wind direction, or both. An important characteristic is that wind shear may be associated with either a wind shift or a wind speed gradient at any level in the atmosphere. Answer (A) is incorrect. Wind shear can be vertical (as well as lateral) in thunderstorm clouds between the updrafts and downdrafts, as well as in other areas such as frontal zones and low-level temperature inversions. Answer (B) is incorrect. Wind shear can be encountered in areas other than thunderstorms, e.g., within a frontal zone, in and near the jet stream, or in low-level inversions.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which is a definition of “severe wind shear”?

choices.text: Any rapid change of horizontal wind shear in excess of 25 knots; vertical shear excepted.
Any rapid change in wind direction or velocity which causes airspeed changes greater than 15 knots or vertical speed changes greater than 500 ft/min.
Any change of airspeed greater than 20 knots which is sustained for more than 20 seconds or vertical speed changes in excess of 100 ft/min.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Severe wind shear는 급격한 풍향·풍속 변화로 airspeed가 15 kt 초과 변하거나 vertical speed가 500 ft/min 초과 변하는 경우를 말한다.
questions.explanation_en: A severe wind shear is defined as a rapid change in wind direction or velocity causing airspeed changes greater than 15 kt. or vertical speed changes greater than 500 ft/min. Answer (A) is incorrect. A severe wind shear can occur with both horizontal and vertical shears. Answer (C) is incorrect. A severe wind shear causes airspeed changes greater than 15 kt., not 20 kt., or vertical speed changes greater than 500 ft/min., not 100 ft/min.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What information from the control tower is indicated by the following transmission? “SOUTH BOUNDARY WIND ONE SIX ZERO AT TWO FIVE, WEST BOUNDARY WIND TWO FOUR ZERO AT THREE FIVE.”

choices.text: A downburst is located at the center of the airport.
Wake turbulence exists on the west side of the active runway.
There is a possibility of wind shear over or near the airport.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. LLWAS는 공항 주변 여러 지점의 바람을 중심부 바람과 비교해 low-level wind shear 가능성을 탐지한다. 차이가 커지면 tower가 해당 위치와 바람을 조종사에게 제공한다.
questions.explanation_en: The information for the transmission was provided by the Low-Level Wind Shear Alert System (LLWAS). This system detects the possibility of low-level wind shear over or near the airport. The system compares the wind measured around the airport with the wind measured at the center field location. When conditions exist, the tower controller will provide the site’s location and wind. Note that the transmission in the question indicates wind from different directions at the airport. Answer (A) is incorrect. A downburst is a vertical movement of air that is not measured by the LLWAS until it has horizontal movement. Also the wind direction is toward the center of the airport, not away from it. Answer (B) is incorrect. Wake turbulence does not produce wind. It is generated by an aircraft that is producing lift, which could be on either side of the active runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What airport condition is reported by the tower when more than one wind condition at different positions on the airport is reported?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Tower가 공항 내 서로 다른 위치에서 두 개 이상의 wind condition을 보고하면 wind shear 가능성이 높다는 뜻이다. 이는 LLWAS 여러 sensor의 풍향·풍속 차이가 커졌기 때문이다.
questions.explanation_en: When the tower reports more than one wind condition at different positions on the airport, it means that wind shear is probable. Various sensors of the Low-Level Wind Shear Alert System measure the wind, and when differences become excessive, the tower will provide more than one wind condition at different positions. Answer (A) is incorrect. Light and variable is used to report the wind conditions when wind speed is less than 5 kt. Answer (C) is incorrect. A frontal passage is normally indicated by a change in wind direction, but it is usually not reported by the tower.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which INITIAL flight deck indications should a pilot be aware of when a headwind shears to a calm wind?

choices.text: Indicated airspeed decreases, aircraft pitches up, and altitude decreases.
Indicated airspeed increases, aircraft pitches down, and altitude increases.
Indicated airspeed decreases, aircraft pitches down, and altitude decreases.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Headwind에서 calm으로 급변하면 headwind component가 감소해 IAS와 성능이 떨어지고, 항공기는 nose-down 경향과 고도손실을 보인다.
questions.explanation_en: As the wind shears from a headwind to a calm wind, there is a quick reduction in the headwind component and a decrease in aircraft performance. The indications will be a decrease in indicated airspeed, a pitch down of the airplane’s nose, and a decrease in altitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. The aircraft will pitch down, not up, due to the relatively small angle of attack used during the headwind and the sudden decrease in the airflow over the wing when the wind shears to calm. Answer (B) is incorrect. Less power is required to maintain an indicated airspeed in a headwind than in calm air because of ram air; thus, a shear from a headwind to calm is indicated by a decrease in airspeed and a decrease, not an increase, in altitude.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which condition would INITIALLY cause the indicated airspeed and pitch to increase and the sink rate to decrease?

choices.text: Sudden decrease in a headwind component.
Tailwind which suddenly increases in velocity.
Sudden increase in a headwind component.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Tailwind에서 headwind로 바뀌는 등 headwind component가 갑자기 증가하면 처음에는 IAS, pitch, altitude가 증가해 성능이 좋아진다.
questions.explanation_en: A sudden increase in a headwind component, i.e., a tailwind shearing to a headwind, is initially indicated by an increase in airspeed, pitch, and altitude. A sudden increase in a headwind component will increase aircraft performance. Answer (A) is incorrect. A sudden decrease in a headwind component decreases aircraft performance and is indicated by a decrease in airspeed, pitch, and altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. An increase in tailwind velocity decreases performance and is indicated by a decrease in airspeed, pitch, and altitude.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which INITIAL flight deck indications should a pilot be aware of when a constant tailwind shears to a calm wind?

choices.text: Altitude increases; pitch and indicated airspeed decrease.
Altitude, pitch, and indicated airspeed decrease.
Altitude, pitch, and indicated airspeed increase.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 일정한 tailwind가 calm으로 바뀌면 상대적으로 IAS가 증가하고 성능이 좋아져 pitch-up 및 고도상승 경향이 나타난다.
questions.explanation_en: When a constant tailwind shears to a calm wind, the shear increases indicated airspeed and thus increases performance. The airplane tends to pitch up and gain altitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. Pitch and indicated airspeed also increase. Answer (B) is incorrect. Altitude, pitch, and indicated airspeed decrease when a headwind, not tailwind, shears to a calm wind.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which wind-shear condition results in an increase in airspeed?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Tailwind가 headwind로 급변하면 초기에는 IAS가 증가하고 항공기가 pitch-up하며 고도가 증가한다.
questions.explanation_en: When a tailwind shears to a headwind, the airspeed initially increases, the aircraft pitches up, and the altitude increases. Answer (A) is incorrect. When a headwind shears to a tailwind, thus increasing the tailwind component and decreasing the headwind component, the reduction of the ram air pressure on the pitot tube causes an initial reduction of indicated airspeed. The reduced headwind component will also cause a pitch down moment and a decrease in altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. When a headwind shears to a tailwind, thus increasing the tailwind component and decreasing the headwind component, the reduction of the ram air pressure on the pitot tube causes an initial reduction of indicated airspeed. The reduced headwind component will also cause a pitch down moment and a decrease in altitude.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which wind-shear condition results in a loss of airspeed?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Headwind component가 감소하거나 tailwind가 증가하면 초기에는 IAS 감소, nose-down 경향, 고도감소가 나타난다.
questions.explanation_en: When the headwind component decreases or the tailwind component increases, initially the airspeed decreases, the aircraft pitches down, and the altitude decreases. Answer (A) is incorrect. In a decreasing tailwind condition, airspeed initially increases, not decreases. Answer (C) is incorrect. Both an increasing headwind and a decreasing tailwind increase, not decrease, airspeed initially.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which airplane performance characteristics should be recognized during takeoff when encountering a tailwind shear that increases in intensity?

choices.text: Loss of, or diminished, airspeed performance.
Increased climb performance immediately after takeoff.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Tailwind shear가 강해질수록 IAS와 항공기 성능이 감소하므로 이를 보상하려면 더 많은 thrust가 필요하다.
questions.explanation_en: As a tailwind shear increases in intensity, the aircraft performance decreases. More power will be required to counter the decrease in airspeed. As the tailwind intensity increases, there will be a loss of, or diminished, airspeed performance. Answer (B) is incorrect. As a tailwind shear increases, takeoff distance is increased, not decreased, because more power or distance is required to attain liftoff speed. Answer (C) is incorrect. As a tailwind shear increases during climbout, the climb performance will decrease, not increase.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Thrust is being managed to maintain desired indicated airspeed and the glide slope is being flown. Which characteristics should be observed when a tailwind shears to a constant headwind?

choices.text: PITCH ATTITUDE: Increases. VERTICAL SPEED: Increases. INDICATED AIRSPEED: Decreases, then increases to approach speed.
PITCH ATTITUDE: Increases. VERTICAL SPEED: Decreases. INDICATED AIRSPEED: Increases, then decreases.
PITCH ATTITUDE: Decreases. VERTICAL SPEED: Decreases. INDICATED AIRSPEED: Decreases, then increases to approach speed.
