questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Tailwind가 일정한 headwind로 바뀌면 IAS는 처음 증가한 뒤 다시 감소할 수 있고 pitch attitude는 증가한다. 처음에는 감속을 위해 thrust를 줄였다가 일정한 headwind에서 glide slope를 유지하려면 다시 thrust를 높이게 된다.
questions.explanation_en: When a tailwind shears to a constant headwind, the indicated airspeed will initially increase, then decrease. The vertical speed will decrease, and pitch attitude will increase. Initially, thrust will be reduced to slow the airspeed, then increased as more power and a slower rate of descent are needed to maintain the glide slope in a constant headwind. Answer (A) is incorrect. Indicated airspeed will initially increase, not decrease, and vertical speed will decrease, not increase. Answer (C) is incorrect. Both pitch and indicated airspeed will initially increase, not decrease.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: In comparison to an approach in a moderate headwind, which is an indication of a possible wind shear due to a decreasing headwind when descending on the glide slope?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Decreasing headwind shear는 IAS와 성능을 낮추고 항공기가 nose-down하려는 경향을 만든다. 회복하려면 더 높은 pitch attitude가 필요하다.
questions.explanation_en: A decreasing headwind shear will decrease indicated airspeed and performance capability. Due to a loss of airspeed, the airplane will tend to pitch down. Thus, a higher pitch attitude is required. Answer (A) is incorrect. As airspeed decreases, more, not less, power is required. Answer (C) is incorrect. As the headwind decreases, groundspeed will increase, requiring a higher, not a lower, descent rate.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the recommended technique to counter the loss of airspeed and resultant lift from wind shear?

choices.text: Lower the pitch attitude and regain lost airspeed.
Avoid overstressing the aircraft, “pitch to airspeed,” and apply maximum power.
Maintain, or increase, pitch attitude and accept the lower-than-normal airspeed indications.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. IAS와 lift가 감소한다면 increasing tailwind 또는 decreasing headwind shear의 징후이다. 회복 시 정상보다 낮은 IAS 표시를 감수하더라도 pitch attitude를 유지하거나 증가시키는 것이 중요하다.
questions.explanation_en: A loss of airspeed and resultant lift indicates an increasing tailwind (or decreasing headwind) shear. Successful recovery from a wind-shear encounter requires maintaining or increasing pitch attitude and accepting lower-than-normal airspeed indications. Answer (A) is incorrect. Lowering the pitch attitude to regain lost airspeed is a result of past training emphasis on airspeed control; it is not the recommended technique for recovering from a wind shear. Answer (B) is incorrect. The recommended technique to recover from a wind shear is to maintain or increase pitch attitude and not “pitch to airspeed,” which may decrease pitch to regain lost airspeed.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When thrust is being used to manage the glide slope, which characteristics should be observed when a headwind shears to a constant tailwind?

choices.text: Decrease in pitch, increase in vertical speed, and loss of airspeed followed by on speed indications.
Decrease in pitch, decrease in vertical speed, and increase in airspeed.
Increase in pitch, decrease in vertical speed, and loss of airspeed.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Increasing tailwind 또는 decreasing headwind shear는 IAS와 성능을 떨어뜨리고 항공기가 trim speed를 되찾으려 nose-down할 수 있으므로 미리 대비해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: In contrast to shears that increase airspeed, an increasing tailwind (or decreasing headwind) shear will decrease indicated airspeed and performance capability. Due to airspeed loss, the airplane may tend to pitch down to regain trim speed. Be prepared! Answer (B) is incorrect. Decrease in pitch and vertical speed with an increase in airspeed would be due to a decreasing tailwind to a headwind shear. Answer (C) is incorrect. Increase in pitch, decrease in vertical speed, and loss of airspeed is a result of a sudden increase in a headwind component.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Turbulence encountered above 15,000 feet AGL, not associated with cloud formations, should be reported as
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 15,000 ft AGL 이상에서 cumuliform cloud와 관계없이 만나는 고고도 난류는 clear-air turbulence(CAT)로 보고한다.
questions.explanation_en: High-level turbulence encountered above 15,000 ft. AGL, not associated with cumuliform cloudiness, should be reported as clear air turbulence. Answer (A) is incorrect. Convective turbulence is normally associated with cumuliform clouds and is reported as turbulence. Answer (B) is incorrect. Turbulence above 15,000 ft. AGL, not associated with clouds, is termed clear air turbulence, not high-altitude turbulence.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is a likely location of clear air turbulences?

choices.text: In an upper trough on the polar side of a jet stream.
Near a ridge aloft on the equatorial side of a high-pressure flow.
Downstream of the equatorial side of a jet stream.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. CAT는 jet stream의 polar side, 특히 깊어지는 upper trough 부근에서 잘 발생한다. 이곳에서는 강한 wind shear와 cold/warm advection이 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: A preferred location of clear air turbulence is in an upper trough on the polar side of the jet stream. Cold and warm advection along with strong wind shears develop near the jet stream, especially where the curvature of the jet stream sharply increases in deepening upper troughs. Answer (B) is incorrect. CAT is likely to occur on the polar side of a jet stream in an upper trough, not near a ridge aloft on the equatorial side of a high-pressure flow. Answer (C) is incorrect. CAT is likely on the polar, not equatorial, side of a jet stream.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What action is appropriate when encountering the first ripple of reported clear air turbulence (CAT)?

choices.text: Extend flaps to decrease wind loading.
Extend gear to provide more drag and increase stability.
Adjust airspeed to that recommended for rough air.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. CAT의 첫 흔들림을 만나면 rough-air recommended speed로 감속하는 것이 적절하며, 이는 난류 중 항공기에 가해지는 구조하중을 줄인다.
questions.explanation_en: When encountering the first ripple of clear air turbulence (CAT), it is appropriate to reduce airspeed to that recommended for rough air. This action decreases the amount of stress that is put on the airplane while in turbulence. Answer (A) is incorrect. Use of flaps increases the camber of the wing and angle of attack but does not decrease the amount of wing loading. Cruise airspeed usually exceeds the flap operating airspeed. This slow airspeed with a higher angle of attack greatly increases the possibility of a stall due to a vertical gust of wind exceeding the airplane’s critical angle of attack. Answer (B) is incorrect. Extending the gear increases the drag but does not change the stability of the airplane. The reduced airspeed to extend the gear requires a higher angle of attack, which may cause the critical angle of attack to be exceeded during a wind shear.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Clear air turbulence (CAT) associated with a mountain wave may extend as far as

choices.text: 1,000 miles or more downstream of the mountain.
100 miles or more upwind of the mountain.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Mountain wave CAT는 산 정상에서 tropopause 위 약 5,000 ft까지, 그리고 산의 downwind 방향으로 100 mi 이상 이어질 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Mountain waves can create clear air turbulence (CAT). Mountain wave CAT may extend from the mountain crests to as high as 5,000 ft. above the tropopause and can range 100 mi. or more downstream from the mountains. Answer (A) is incorrect. Mountain wave CAT can range 100, not 1,000, mi. or more downstream of the mountain. Answer (C) is incorrect. Mountain wave CAT is downwind, not upwind, of the mountain.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Under what conditions would clear air turbulence (CAT) most likely be encountered?

choices.text: When constant pressure charts show 20-knot isotachs less than 60 NM apart.
When constant pressure charts show 60-knot isotachs less than 20 NM apart.
When a sharp trough is moving at a speed less than 20 knots.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Constant pressure chart에서 20-kt isotach 간격이 60 NM 미만이면 CAT를 일으킬 충분한 horizontal shear가 있는 것으로 본다. 주로 jet stream의 polar side에서 나타난다.
questions.explanation_en: When constant pressure charts show 20-kt. isotachs less than 60 NM apart, there is sufficient horizontal shear for CAT. These conditions normally occur on the polar side of the jet stream. Answer (B) is incorrect. When constant pressure charts show 20-kt., not 60-kt., isotachs less than 60 NM, not 20 NM, apart, CAT is most likely to be encountered. Answer (C) is incorrect. CAT can be expected upwind of the base of a deep upper trough, not because a sharp trough is moving.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: If severe turbulence is encountered, which procedure is recommended?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Severe turbulence에서는 일정고도를 억지로 유지하려는 조작이 구조하중을 크게 늘린다. 일정한 attitude를 유지하고 updraft/downdraft에 따라 고도가 변하도록 두는 편이 하중을 줄인다.
questions.explanation_en: When severe turbulence is encountered, as in a thunderstorm, it is almost impossible to hold a constant altitude. Maneuvering in an attempt to do so greatly increases stress on the aircraft. Stresses will be least if the aircraft is held in a constant attitude and allowed to ride the waves of updrafts and downdrafts. Answer (A) is incorrect. Severe turbulence causes large abrupt changes in altitude, and attempting to hold a constant altitude may overstress the airplane. Answer (C) is incorrect. Severe turbulence causes large variations in both indicated airspeed and altitude. Any attempt to maintain constant airspeed and altitude may overstress the aircraft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What action is recommended when encountering turbulence due to a wind shift associated with a sharp pressure trough?

choices.text: Establish a straight course across the storm area.
Climb or descend to a smoother level.
Increase speed to get out of the trough as soon as possible.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Sharp pressure trough line과 관련된 급격한 wind shift에서 난류를 만나면 storm area를 가로질러 직선으로 통과하는 것이 좋다. 난류대가 보통 trough와 평행하므로 통과 시간을 줄일 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: If turbulence is encountered in an abrupt wind shift associated with a sharp pressure trough line, you should establish a straight course across the storm area. This action is recommended because the turbulence normally is parallel to the trough and by crossing the storm area you will minimize the turbulence. Answer (B) is incorrect. Climbing or descending to a smoother level is recommended when encountering jet stream turbulence with direct tailwinds or headwinds, not because of a wind shift associated with a sharp pressure trough. Answer (C) is incorrect. Speed should be decreased, not increased, to the recommended airspeed for rough air to avoid over-stressing the airplane.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which action is recommended if jet stream turbulence is encountered with a direct headwind or tailwind?

choices.text: Increase airspeed to get out of the area quickly.
Change course to fly on the polar side of the jet stream.
Change altitude or course to avoid a possible elongated turbulent area.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 직접적인 headwind 또는 tailwind를 동반한 jet-stream turbulence를 만나면 고도나 course를 바꾸는 것이 좋다. 이런 난류대는 바람 방향으로 길고 수직으로 얕고 좁다.
questions.explanation_en: If jet stream turbulence with direct tailwinds or headwinds is encountered, a change of altitude or course should be initiated since these turbulent areas are elongated with the wind and are shallow and narrow. Answer (A) is incorrect. An increase in airspeed may overstress the airplane in turbulent conditions. Normally, a reduction in airspeed is required for turbulent air penetration. Answer (B) is incorrect. CAT is normally on the polar side of the jet stream, so you would be flying into more turbulent weather.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which action is recommended regarding an altitude change to get out of jet stream turbulence?

choices.text: Descend if ambient temperature is falling.
Descend if ambient temperature is rising.
Maintain altitude if ambient temperature is not changing.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Sloping tropopause 관련 turbulence에서는 기온 변화를 관찰한다. 가장 낮은 온도 지점이 tropopause 통과점이며, stratospheric side의 temperature-change zone에서 난류가 더 강하다. 기온이 내려가면 강하, 올라가면 상승하면 난류대 이탈에 도움이 된다.
questions.explanation_en: If turbulence is due to a sloping tropopause, watch the temperature gauge. The point of coldest temperature will be the tropopause penetration. Turbulence will be more pronounced in the temperature-change zone on the stratospheric (upper) side of the sloping tropopause. To get out of this turbulence, descend if the ambient temperature is falling, and climb with a rising temperature. Answer (B) is incorrect. To get out of jet stream turbulence with a rising ambient temperature, you would climb, not descend. Answer (C) is incorrect. You would need to make an altitude change due to jet stream turbulence, and there should be a temperature change due to a sloping tropopause.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: You can expect turbulence when winds exceed
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 험준한 산악을 넘을 때 산을 가로지르는 풍속이 약 40 kt를 초과하면 severe turbulence 가능성을 예상해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: When flying over rugged hills or mountains, you may encounter severe turbulence. Anticipate turbulence when wind speed across mountains exceeds about 40 knots. Answer (A) is incorrect. While winds blowing up or down mountain slopes could cause turbulence, the FAA guidance in AC 00-06A specifically references wind blowing across mountains in excess of 40 knots as favorable conditions for turbulence. Answer (B) is incorrect. While winds blowing up or down mountain slopes could cause turbulence, the FAA guidance in AC 00-06A specifically references wind blowing across mountains in excess of 40 knots as favorable conditions for turbulence.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The threshold windspeed in the jet stream for clear air turbulence is generally considered to be
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Jet stream에서 CAT 가능성을 고려하는 기준풍속은 약 110 kt이다. 그러나 CAT를 직접 만드는 것은 풍속 자체보다 고도·위치 간 풍속차, 즉 wind shear이다.
questions.explanation_en: The threshold windspeed in the jet stream for clear air turbulence (CAT) is considered to be 110 knots. Windspeed in jet streams can be much stronger than 110 knots, and the probability of encountering CAT increases proportionally with the windspeed and the wind shear it generates. It is not the wind speed itself that causes CAT. It is the wind shear, or difference in windspeed from one level or point to another, that causes the wave motion or overturning in the atmosphere that is turbulence to an aircraft. Answer (A) is incorrect. The threshold windspeed in the jet stream for CAT is considered to be 110 knots. Answer (C) is incorrect. Windspeed in jet streams can be much stronger than 110 knots, and the probability of encountering CAT increases proportionally with the windspeed and the wind shear it generates. It is not the wind speed itself that causes CAT. It is the wind shear, or difference in windspeed from one level or point to another, that causes the wave motion or overturning in the atmosphere that is turbulence to an aircraft. The given number of knots for the threshold windspeed in the jet stream is 110 knots.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Clear air turbulence (CAT) can be found
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. CAT는 기본적으로 convective cloud 밖에서 만나는 난류이며 cirrus 및 standing lenticular cloud 내부·주변 난류도 포함해 표현한다.
questions.explanation_en: Clear air turbulence (CAT) is best defined as turbulence encountered outside of convective clouds. The term CAT is used to describe the turbulence within and in the vicinity of cirrus and standing lenticular clouds. Answer (B) is incorrect. CAT implies turbulence devoid of clouds. However, we commonly reserve the term for high level wind shear turbulence, even when in cirrus clouds. Answer (C) is incorrect. CAT is associated with upper level fronts and jet streams and is not intended to predict turbulence associated with breaking mountain waves or other terrain features.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Moderate CAT is considered likely when the vertical wind shear is

choices.text: 15 knots per 2,000 feet or greater and/or the horizontal wind shear is 40 knots per 150 miles or greater.
10 knots per 1,000 feet or greater and/or the horizontal wind shear is 50 knots per 150 miles or greater.
5 knots per 1,000 feet or greater and/or the horizontal wind shear is 40 knots per 150 miles or greater.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Moderate CAT 가능성은 vertical wind shear가 1,000 ft당 5 kt 이상 및/또는 horizontal shear가 150 mi당 40 kt 이상일 때 높아진다.
questions.explanation_en: Wind shear occurs in all directions, but, for convenience, it is measured along vertical and horizontal axes, thus becoming horizontal and vertical wind shear. Moderate clear air turbulence (CAT) is considered likely when the vertical wind shear is 5 knots per 1,000 feet or greater and/or the horizontal wind shear is 40 knots per 150 miles or greater. Answer (A) is incorrect. Moderate CAT is considered likely when the vertical wind shear is 5 knots per 1,000 feet or greater and/or the horizontal wind shear is 40 knots per 150 miles or greater. Answer (B) is incorrect. Moderate CAT is considered likely when the vertical wind shear is 5 knots per 1,000 feet or greater and/or the horizontal wind shear is 40 knots per 150 miles or greater.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When encountering severe turbulence, you should

choices.text: Slow to turbulent air penetration speed.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Severe turbulence를 만나면 turbulent-air penetration speed 또는 VA로 감속해야 한다. 더 빠른 속도에서는 난류·조작 시 구조하중이 과도해질 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: When encountering severe turbulence, you should slow down to turbulent air penetration speed, maneuvering speed (VA). A faster airspeed could cause excessive stress on the aircraft when maneuvering. Answer (B) is incorrect. Severe turbulence causes large variations in both indicated airspeed and altitude. Any attempt to maintain constant airspeed and altitude may overstress the aircraft. Answer (C) is incorrect. Severe turbulence causes large abrupt changes in altitude, and attempting to hold a constant altitude may overstress the airplane.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which is one of the three key elements in an effective clear air turbulence (CAT) Avoidance System?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 효과적인 CAT 회피체계의 핵심은 적절한 초기·정기 훈련, 전담 planning/dispatch 기능, 그리고 충분히 지원되는 PIREP/communications 체계이다.
questions.explanation_en: There are three key elements in an effective CAT avoidance system: (1) an appropriate initial and recurrent training program, (2) a dedicated planning/dispatch function, and (3) a fully supported operational implementation of a PIREP/ communications system (not ATC-based). Answer (A) is incorrect. There is appropriate initial training and a recurrent training program. Answer (B) is incorrect. CAT is not ATC-based.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the expected duration of an individual microburst?

choices.text: Five minutes with maximum winds lasting approximately 2 to 4 minutes.
One microburst may continue for as long as an hour.
Seldom longer than 15 minutes from the time the burst strikes the ground until dissipation.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 개별 microburst는 지면 도달부터 소멸까지 보통 15분을 넘지 않는다. 수평풍은 첫 5분 동안 증가하며 최대강도는 약 2~4분 지속된다.
questions.explanation_en: An individual microburst will seldom last longer than 15 min. from the time it strikes the ground until dissipation. The horizontal winds continue to increase during the first 5 min., with maximum-intensity winds lasting approximately 2 to 4 min. Answer (A) is incorrect. Individual microbursts seldom last longer than 15 min., not 5 min. Answer (B) is incorrect. When microbursts are concentrated into a line structure (not an individual microburst), activity may continue for as long as 1 hr.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Maximum downdrafts in a microburst encounter may be as strong as
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Microburst downdraft는 6,000 ft/min까지 강할 수 있고 지면 부근 수평풍은 45 kt에 달해 headwind-tailwind 사이 총 90 kt wind shear를 만들 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Downdrafts in a microburst can be as strong as 6,000 ft/min. Horizontal winds near the surface can be as strong as 45 kt., resulting in a 90-kt. wind shear. The strong horizontal winds occur within a few hundred feet of the ground. Answer (A) is incorrect. Maximum downdrafts in a microburst may be as strong as 6,000, not 8,000, ft/min. Answer (B) is incorrect. Maximum downdrafts in a microburst may be as strong as 6,000, not 7,000, ft/min.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Maximum downdrafts in a microburst encounter may be as strong as
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Microburst는 최대 약 6,000 fpm downdraft와 지면 부근 45 kt 수평풍을 만들 수 있어 약 90 kt의 wind shear가 발생할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Downdrafts in a microburst can be as strong as 6,000 ft/min. Horizontal winds near the surface can be as strong as 45 kt., resulting in a 90-kt. wind shear. The strong horizontal winds occur within a few hundred feet of the ground. Answer (A) is incorrect. Maximum downdrafts in a microburst may be as strong as 6,000, not 1,500, ft/min. Answer (B) is incorrect. Maximum downdrafts in a microburst may be as strong as 6,000, not 4,500, ft/min.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the expected duration of an individual microburst?

choices.text: Two minutes with maximum winds lasting approximately 1 minute.
One microburst may continue for as long as 2 to 4 hours.
Seldom longer than 15 minutes from the time the burst strikes the ground until dissipation.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Microburst의 전체 수명은 보통 15분 이내이며 첫 5분에 수평풍이 강화되고 최대풍은 약 2~4분 유지된다.
questions.explanation_en: An individual microburst will seldom last longer than 15 min. from the time it strikes ground until dissipation. The horizontal winds continue to increase during the first 5 min., with maximum-intensity winds lasting approximately 2 to 4 min. Answer (A) is incorrect. Microbursts last 15, not 2 min., and maximum winds last 2 to 4 min., not 1 min. Answer (B) is incorrect. The maximum winds last 2 to 4 min., not 2 to 4 hr., and the microburst is usually limited to about 15 min.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Doppler wind measurements indicate that the windspeed change a pilot may expect when flying through the peak intensity of a microburst is approximately
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 평균 microburst의 최대강도 지점을 통과할 때 약 45 kt의 wind-speed change가 예상되지만 실제로는 거의 100 kt 차이가 관측된 사례도 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Doppler radar wind measurements indicate that the wind speed change a pilot might expect when flying through the average microburst at its point of peak intensity is about 45 kt. However, microburst wind speed differences of almost 100 kt. have been measured. Answer (A) is incorrect. A pilot may expect a 45-kt., not a 15-kt., wind speed change when flying through the peak intensity of a microburst. Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot may expect a 45-kt., not a 25-kt., wind speed change when flying through the peak intensity of a microburst.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: An aircraft that encounters a headwind of 45 knots, within a microburst, may expect a total shear across the microburst of
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Microburst 한쪽의 headwind가 45 kt라면 반대쪽에는 약 45 kt tailwind가 있을 수 있어 통과 항공기는 총 90 kt shear를 경험할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: If a headwind in a microburst is 45 kt., the wind will be going in the opposite direction on the other side of the microburst at presumably the same 45 kt., resulting in a wind shear between the headwind and tailwind of 90 kt. Answer (A) is incorrect. The total shear is the total headwind to tailwind change of a traversing aircraft; thus a 45-kt. headwind would shear 90 kt., not 40 kt., to a 45-kt. tailwind. Answer (B) is incorrect. The total shear is the total headwind to tailwind change of a traversing aircraft; thus a 45-kt. headwind would shear 90 kt., not 80 kt., to a 45-kt. tailwind.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: An aircraft that encounters a headwind of 40 knots, within a microburst, may expect a total shear across the microburst of
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Microburst에서 headwind 40 kt에서 반대편 tailwind 40 kt로 바뀌면 총 wind shear는 약 80 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: If a headwind in a microburst is 40 kt., the wind will be going in the opposite direction on the other side of a microburst at presumably the same 40 kt., resulting in an 80-kt. shear (headwind to tailwind change for a traversing aircraft) across the microburst. Answer (A) is incorrect. The total shear is the total headwind to tailwind change of a traversing airplane; thus, a 40-kt. headwind would shear 80 kt., not 40 kt., to a 40-kt. tailwind. Answer (C) is incorrect. The total shear is the total headwind to tailwind change of a traversing airplane; thus, a 40-kt. headwind would shear 80 kt., not 90 kt., to a 40-kt. tailwind.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: As you approach an airport to land, you observe a convective cloud over the airport with virga below it. This could indicate
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Virga는 강수가 지면에 닿기 전에 증발하는 현상이다. 증발냉각으로 주변 공기가 차갑고 무거워져 강한 downdraft와 때로 microburst를 만들 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Rain that falls through the atmosphere but evaporates prior to striking the ground is known as virga. The process of evaporation cools the air around the virga and can create strong downdrafts and in some cases microbursts. Answer (A) is incorrect. Virga is often associated with strong downdrafts due to the cooling effect of evaporation. Therefore, the air around virga would be very turbulent, not smooth. Answer (B) is incorrect. Virga occurs when precipitation is not able to penetrate a layer of dry air and evaporates before it reaches the surface. Thus, heavy rain showers would not be indicated by virga.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 144 on page 851.) If involved in a microburst encounter, in which aircraft positions will the most severe downdraft occur?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Microburst의 가장 강한 downdraft는 중심부에서 나타나며 Fig. 144의 position 3과 4가 이에 해당한다.
questions.explanation_en: The most severe downdrafts occur at the center of the microburst, indicated by positions 3 and 4 in Fig. 144. Answer (A) is incorrect. Position 5 has significantly less downdraft even though it has considerably more tailwind. Answer (B) is incorrect. Position 2 does not have as significant a downdraft as 3 and 4, but it contains a significant headwind even though it is decreasing.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 144 on page 851.) What effect will a microburst encounter have upon the aircraft in position 3?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 144 position 3에서는 microburst 중심부에 접근하며 강한 downdraft를 만나고 있다.
questions.explanation_en: At position 3 in Fig. 144, the airplane is experiencing a strong downdraft as it is approaching the center of the microburst. Answer (A) is incorrect. At position 2, not 3, the airplane encounters decreasing headwind. Answer (B) is incorrect. At position 5, the airplane encounters an increasing tailwind, and it may result in an extreme situation as pictured, i.e., just before impact.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 144 on page 851.) What effect will a microburst encounter have upon the aircraft in position 4?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 144 position 4에서는 강한 downdraft와 tailwind를 동시에 만나 항공기 성능이 크게 감소한다.
questions.explanation_en: At position 4 in Fig. 144, the airplane is encountering a strong tailwind in addition to a strong downdraft and a decrease in airplane performance. Answer (B) is incorrect. Updrafts will occur in thunderstorms, not in microbursts from thunderstorms. Answer (C) is incorrect. The significant increase in performance occurs at position 1 where the headwind component is the greatest.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 144 below.) When penetrating a microburst, which aircraft will experience an increase in performance without a change in pitch or power?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 144 position 1은 microburst에 처음 진입해 headwind가 가장 강해지는 지점으로, pitch나 power 변화 없이도 IAS와 성능이 증가한다.
questions.explanation_en: Position 1 on Fig. 144 indicates the position where the airplane first encounters a headwind and experiences increasing performance. This position is where the headwind component is the greatest, providing an increase in performance without a change in pitch or power. Answer (A) is incorrect. Position 3 indicates the point where the most severe downdraft occurs, which results in a decrease in performance. Answer (B) is incorrect. Position 2 does not have as significant a headwind component as position 1; thus, performance is less than at position 1.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 144 below.) How will the aircraft in position 4 be affected by a microburst encounter?

choices.text: Performance increasing with a tailwind and updraft.
Performance decreasing with a tailwind and downdraft.
Performance decreasing with a headwind and downdraft.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 144 position 4에서는 tailwind와 downdraft 때문에 항공기 성능이 감소한다.
questions.explanation_en: The aircraft at position 4 on Fig. 144 is affected by the microburst’s causing a decrease in airplane performance due to a tailwind and downdraft. Answer (A) is incorrect. Performance will decrease, not increase, with a tailwind, and thunderstorms, not microbursts, have updrafts. Answer (C) is incorrect. The airplane at position 2 on Fig. 144 indicates the position where performance will decrease due to a headwind and downdraft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 144 below.) On final approach to the airport, airplane in position #5 would experience
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Tailwind 증가 시 groundspeed는 증가하지만 IAS와 lift는 감소하므로 stall, 고도손실, runway undershoot 위험이 생길 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Groundspeed will increase while indicated airspeed and lift will decrease, potentially leading to a stall with loss of altitude and landing short of the runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. The outflow and increased tailwind will increase groundspeed and can be a means for flight crew to identify wind shear potential. Answer (B) is incorrect. The downdraft component has decreased while the tailwind component has increased. urst Section Chart.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Hazardous vortex turbulence that might be encountered behind large aircraft is created only when that aircraft is
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 날개 위 낮은 압력과 아래 높은 압력의 차이 때문에 공기가 wingtip 주위로 말려 올라가며 뒤쪽으로 두 개의 반대방향 회전 vortex가 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: Lift is generated by the creation of a pressure differential over the wing’s, or other airfoil’s, surface. The lowest pressure occurs over the upper wing surface and the highest pressure under the wing. This pressure differential triggers the roll up of the airflow aft of the wing resulting in swirling air masses trailing downstream from the wingtips. An airplane’s wake consists of two counter-rotating vortices. Answer (B) is incorrect. Hazardous vortex turbulence is created only when that aircraft is developing lift, which can be while operating at low or high airspeeds. A slow, heavy, and clean airplane will generate the most hazardous vortex turbulence. Answer (C) is incorrect. Most takeoff rolls are at high power settings, but the generation of vortices does not occur until lift is produced. Also landing approaches are conducted at lower power settings; vortex turbulence is produced whenever an airplane is producing lift.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How does the wake turbulence vortex circulate around each wingtip?

choices.text: Inward, upward, and around the wingtip.
Counterclockwise when viewed from behind the aircraft.
Outward, upward, and around the wingtip.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 날개 아래의 높은 압력 공기는 wingtip 바깥쪽·위쪽으로 이동해 위쪽의 낮은 압력 영역으로 말려 들어간다.
questions.explanation_en: Because the pressure differential is caused by a lower pressure above the wing and a higher pressure below the wing, the air from the bottom moves out, up, and around each wingtip. Answer (A) is incorrect. The air moves out around the edge of the wing, not in underneath the wing. Answer (B) is incorrect. The air moves out around the edge of the wing. From behind, the left wingtip vortex is clockwise, and the right wingtip vortex is counterclockwise.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which statement is true concerning the wake turbulence produced by a large transport aircraft?

choices.text: Vortices can be avoided by flying 300 feet below and behind the flight path of the generating aircraft.
The vortex characteristics of any given aircraft may be altered by extending the flaps or changing the speed.
Wake turbulence behind a propeller-driven aircraft is negligible because jet engine thrust is a necessary factor in the formation of vortices.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Wake turbulence 강도는 발생 항공기의 weight, speed, wing shape에 좌우되며 flap 등 wing configuration과 속도 변화에 따라 vortex 특성이 달라진다.
questions.explanation_en: The strength of the wake turbulence produced by a large transport aircraft is governed by the weight, speed, and shape of the wing of the generating aircraft. The vortex characteristics of any given aircraft may be altered by the extension of flaps or other wing-configuring devices, as well as a change in speed. Answer (A) is incorrect. The vortices generated by large transport aircraft tend to sink below and behind; thus, vortices can be expected, not avoided, by flying 300 ft. below and behind the flight path of the generating aircraft. Answer (C) is incorrect. Wake turbulence vortices are generated by lift produced by any airplane. It does not matter whether the airplane is powered by propeller or jet engines.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which flight conditions of a large jet airplane create the most severe flight hazard by generating wingtip vortices of the greatest strength?

choices.text: Heavy, slow, gear and flaps up.
Heavy, slow, gear and flaps down.
Heavy, fast, gear and flaps down.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 가장 강한 wingtip vortex는 항공기가 heavy, slow, clean(gear/flaps up) 상태일 때 발생한다.
questions.explanation_en: The strength of a vortex is governed by the weight, speed, and shape of the wing of the generating aircraft. The vortex characteristics of any aircraft can be changed by extension of flaps and landing gear, as well as by changes in speed. The greatest vortex strength of a large jet airplane occurs when the airplane is heavy, slow, and clean (gear and flaps up). Answer (B) is incorrect. The greatest vortex strength occurs when the airplane is heavy and slow with gear and flaps up, not down. Answer (C) is incorrect. The greatest vortex strength occurs when the airplane is heavy and slow, not fast, with gear and flaps up, not down.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Wingtip vortices created by large aircraft tend to

choices.text: sink below the aircraft generating the turbulence.
rise from the surface to traffic pattern altitude.
accumulate and remain for a period of time at the point where the takeoff roll began.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 대형항공기의 vortex는 뒤쪽에서 분당 수백 ft로 가라앉다가 시간·거리와 함께 약해진다. 선행 항공기 flight path 이상에서 비행하고 그 뒤·아래를 피해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The vortices created by large aircraft sink at a rate of several hundred feet per minute, slowing their descent and diminishing in strength with time and distance behind the generating aircraft. Pilots should fly at or above the preceding aircraft’s flight path, avoiding the area behind and below the vortex-generating aircraft. Answer (B) is incorrect. Vortices created by large aircraft tend to sink, not rise, into the traffic pattern altitude. Answer (C) is incorrect. Wingtip vortices are not generated until the aircraft’s wings develop lift, so no wingtip vortices are generated at the point where the takeoff roll begins.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What effect would a light crosswind have on the wingtip vortices generated by a large airplane that has just taken off?

choices.text: The upwind vortex will tend to remain on the runway longer than the downwind vortex.
A crosswind will rapidly dissipate the strength of both vortices.
The downwind vortex will tend to remain on the runway longer than the upwind vortex.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Vortex가 지면 약 200 ft 이내로 내려오면 각 wing 방향으로 지상에서 약 2~3 kt로 옆으로 이동한다. Crosswind에서는 downwind vortex는 빨리 날아가지만 upwind vortex는 활주로에 더 오래 남는다.
questions.explanation_en: When vortices of large aircraft sink close to the ground (within about 200 ft.), they tend to move laterally over the ground at a speed of about 2 or 3 kt. in the direction of each generating wing. Thus, the downwind vortex on a crosswind is blown away quickly, but the upwind vortex remains on the runway longer. Answer (B) is incorrect. A crosswind will hold the upwind vortex in the vicinity of the runway. Answer (C) is incorrect. The downwind vortex moves away at a faster rate than the upwind vortex.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What wind condition prolongs the hazards of wake turbulence on a landing runway for the longest period of time?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 약한 quartering tailwind는 선행기의 vortex를 touchdown zone 앞으로 밀고 upwind vortex를 활주로에 오래 남게 할 수 있어 특히 위험하다.
questions.explanation_en: Light quartering tailwinds require the maximum caution because they can move the vortices of preceding aircraft forward into the touchdown zone and hold the upwind vortex on the runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. Even though a direct tailwind can move the vortices of a preceding aircraft forward into the touchdown zone, it is not as hazardous because both vortices would move to the sides and not remain on the runway. Answer (C) is incorrect. A light quartering headwind would move the vortices away, i.e., toward the runway threshold, from, not into, the touchdown zone on a landing runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: To avoid the wingtip vortices of a departing jet airplane during takeoff, the pilot should

choices.text: lift off at a point well past the jet airplane’s flight path.
climb above and stay upwind of the jet airplane’s flight path.
remain below the flight path of the jet airplane.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 출발 jet의 rotation point부터 강한 vortex가 생성된다. 뒤따라 이륙할 때는 그 지점보다 먼저 rotate하고 선행 jet의 flight path보다 위쪽·upwind에 머물며 뒤·아래를 가로지르는 heading을 피한다.
questions.explanation_en: A departing jet airplane’s rotation point is where full vortices are first generated. On your takeoff, rotate prior to that point. Climb above and remain upwind of the jet airplane’s flight path to avoid the descending wingtip vortices. Avoid subsequent headings which will cross below and behind the jet airplane (i.e., the jet will climb faster than a propeller airplane). Answer (A) is incorrect. If you rotate beyond the jet’s rotation point, you will have to fly up into the jet’s vortices. Answer (C) is incorrect. The jet airplane’s vortices will sink. If you stay below the jet’s flight path, you will fly in the area of the vortices.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: If you take off behind a heavy jet that has just landed, you should plan to lift off

choices.text: prior to the point where the jet touched down.
beyond the point where the jet touched down.
at the point where the jet touched down and on the upwind edge of the runway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 방금 착륙한 heavy jet 뒤에서 이륙할 때는 최소 2분 간격을 두고, 선행기의 touchdown point보다 뒤쪽에서 lift off하도록 계획한다. Nose gear가 접지해 lift가 사라지면 vortex 생성도 끝난다.
questions.explanation_en: You should ensure that an interval of at least 2 min. has elapsed before your takeoff behind a heavy jet that has just landed. Note the point where the heavy jet touched down and plan to lift off beyond that point. The vortices developed by the heavy jet will no longer be generated when lift is no longer produced (which is at the point of touchdown of the jet’s nose gear). Answer (A) is incorrect. A liftoff prior to the point where the jet touched down would force you to climb through the jet’s vortices. Answer (C) is incorrect. Liftoff should be planned beyond, not at, the point of touchdown to ensure you avoid the vortices, and you should remain on the center, not upwind edge, of the runway during takeoff.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: To allow pilots of in-trail lighter aircraft to make flight path adjustments to avoid wake turbulence, pilots of heavy and large jet aircraft should fly

choices.text: below the established glidepath and slightly to either side of the on-course centerline.
on the established glidepath and on the approach course centerline or runway centerline extended.
above the established glidepath and slightly downwind of the on-course centerline.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 강한 wake를 만드는 heavy/large jet은 뒤따르는 경항공기가 회피할 수 있도록 established glide path와 approach course centerline 또는 runway extended centerline을 따라 비행해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: To allow pilots of in-trail lighter aircraft to make flight path adjustments to avoid wake turbulence, pilots of aircraft that produce strong wake vortices, which include heavy and large jet aircraft, should fly on the established glide path and on the approach course centerline or the extended centerline of the runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. Pilots of heavy and large jet aircraft should fly on, not below, the established glide path and on the approach course centerline, not to either side of the centerline. Answer (C) is incorrect. Pilots of heavy and large jet aircraft should fly on, not above, the established glide path and on the approach course centerline, not slightly downwind of the centerline.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Your flight takes you in the path of a large aircraft. In order to avoid the vortices you should fly

choices.text: at the same altitude as the large aircraft.
below the altitude of the large aircraft.
above the flight path of the large aircraft.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 대형항공기 뒤에서는 선행기의 flight path 이상을 유지해야 한다. Wingtip vortex는 아래로 가라앉으므로 선행기 뒤·아래에서 가장 위험하다.
questions.explanation_en: When flying behind a large aircraft, stay at or above the other aircraft’s flight path. Wingtip vortex turbulence tends to sink into the flight path of airplanes operating below the airplane generating the turbulence. Answer (A) is incorrect. In order to avoid the vortices, avoid flying through another aircraft’s flight path. Answer (B) is incorrect. Wingtip vortex turbulence tends to sink into the flight path of airplanes operating below the airplane generating the turbulence.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Hypoxia is the result of which of these conditions?

choices.text: Excessive carbon dioxide in the bloodstream.
Limited oxygen reaching the heart muscles.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Hypoxia는 뇌와 다른 장기의 기능을 떨어뜨릴 정도로 몸에 산소가 부족한 상태이다.
questions.explanation_en: Hypoxia is a state of oxygen deficiency in the body sufficient to impair functions of the brain and other organs. Answer (B) is incorrect. Insufficient, not excessive, carbon dioxide in the blood stream describes hyperventilation, not hypoxia. Answer (C) is incorrect. Hypoxia is insufficient oxygen to the brain, not limited oxygen to the heart muscles.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: What causes hypoxia?

choices.text: Excessive carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
An increase in nitrogen content of the air at high altitudes.
A decrease of oxygen partial pressure.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 고도 노출에 의한 hypoxia는 고도에서 barometric pressure가 낮아져 폐가 흡수할 수 있는 산소량이 줄어들기 때문에 발생한다.
questions.explanation_en: Hypoxia from exposure to altitude is due only to the reduced barometric pressures encountered at altitude. The decrease in barometric pressure makes oxygen less absorbable by the lungs. Answer (A) is incorrect. The percentage of carbon dioxide and oxygen in the atmosphere remains constant with changes in altitude. There is just less pressure as you increase in altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. Relative nitrogen content remains constant at high altitudes. There is just less pressure.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Loss of cabin pressure may result in hypoxia because as cabin altitude increases

choices.text: the percentage of nitrogen in the air is increased.
the percentage of oxygen in the air is decreased.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 고도가 높아질수록 대기압이 낮아져 산소의 partial pressure가 감소하고 폐에서 흡수되는 산소량도 줄어 hypoxia가 발생한다.
questions.explanation_en: Hypoxia from exposure to altitude is due only to the reduced barometric pressures encountered at altitude. With the decrease in barometric pressure, less oxygen is absorbable by the lungs. Answer (A) is incorrect. The percentage of nitrogen, carbon dioxide, and oxygen in the atmosphere remains constant with changes in altitude. There is just less pressure as you increase in altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. Oxygen remains at about 21% in the atmosphere, i.e., from the ground out to space. The amount of oxygen decreases, however, due to lower barometric pressure.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: A pilot making a blood donation in order to help a sick associate should be aware that for several weeks

choices.text: sufficient oxygen may not reach the cells in the body.
fewer oxygen molecules will be available to the respiratory membranes.
the ability of the body tissues to effectively use oxygen is decreased.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 헌혈 후에는 산소를 운반할 혈액량이 부족해져 hypemic hypoxia가 발생할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Blood donations can cause hypemic hypoxia due to the fact that not enough blood is available to carry a sufficient amount of oxygen to the cells. Answer (B) is incorrect. The amount of oxygen available to the body does not change; however, there may not be enough blood to carry the oxygen to the cells. Answer (C) is incorrect. The body tissues have not lost the ability to use oxygen; however, the amount of blood available to deliver the oxygen has decreased.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: What is a symptom of carbon monoxide poisoning?

choices.text: Pain and cramping of the hands and feet.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Carbon monoxide poisoning의 대표 증상은 두통, 졸림, 어지러움이며, 항공기에서는 고장 난 cabin heater가 원인이 될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning include headache, drowsiness, and dizziness. Pilots should be alert to the possibility that they may be experiencing carbon monoxide poisoning. Carbon monoxide poisoning generally occurs as a result of a defective cabin heater. Answer (A) is incorrect. Rapid breathing can result in hyperventilation, but it is not a symptom of carbon monoxide poisoning. Answer (B) is incorrect. Tingling, not pain and cramping, in the extremities is one symptom of hyperventilation, not carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: What is the effect of alcohol consumption on functions of the body?

choices.text: Alcohol has an adverse effect, especially as altitude increases.
Alcohol has little effect if followed by an ounce of black coffee for every ounce of alcohol.
Small amounts of alcohol in the human system increase judgment and decision-making abilities.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Alcohol은 비행능력을 떨어뜨리고 소량이라도 spatial disorientation과 hypoxia에 더 취약하게 만든다.
questions.explanation_en: Alcohol impairs flying skills. Even small amounts of alcohol render pilots more susceptible to disorientation and hypoxia. Answer (B) is incorrect. There is no way, including drinking black coffee, to increase the body’s metabolism of alcohol or cure a hangover. Answer (C) is incorrect. Even small amounts of alcohol impair, not increase, judgment and decision-making abilities.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Pilots should remember the alcohol in one beer can be detected for as long as
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 맥주 한 병 정도의 alcohol도 최소 약 3시간 동안 호흡이나 혈액에서 검출될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The alcohol consumed in one beer is detectable in the breath or blood for at least 3 hours. Answer (A) is incorrect. The alcohol consumed in one beer is detectable in the breath or blood for at least 3 hours, not 2 hours. Answer (C) is incorrect. The alcohol consumed in one beer is detectable in the breath or blood for at least 3 hours, not for 4 hours.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Pilots should know

choices.text: it takes a minimum of four ounces of liquor to cause impairment.
as little as one beer can cause impairment.
it takes a minimum of eight ounces of wine to cause impairment.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 맥주 한 병 정도의 적은 alcohol도 비행능력을 저하시킬 수 있고 최소 약 3시간 동안 검출될 수 있다. 규정상 '8 hours bottle to throttle'을 기억해야 하며 안전상 12~24시간 이상의 간격이 더 바람직하다.
questions.explanation_en: Extensive research has provided a number of facts about the hazards of alcohol consumption and flying. As little as one bottle of beer can impair flying skills, and the alcohol consumed in these drinks is detectable in the breath and blood for at least 3 hours after drinking. Always remember, “8 hours from bottle to throttle,” though it is much safer to allow at least 12 to 24 hours between “bottle and throttle.” Answer (A) is incorrect. It takes a minimum of one ounce of liquor to cause impairment. Answer (C) is incorrect. It takes a minimum of four ounces of wine to cause impairment.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Consumption of alcohol

choices.text: can severely impair a person for more than 8 hours.
is of no concern in aviation after 8 hours regardless of amount consumed.
in small amounts has no effect on judgment and decision-making.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 적당량의 alcohol도 대사가 느려 8시간 뒤까지 영향을 줄 수 있고, 혈중 alcohol이 사라진 뒤에도 hangover로 수행능력이 오랫동안 저하될 수 있다. 최소 8시간 규정을 지키고 가능하면 12~24시간 간격을 두는 것이 안전하다.
questions.explanation_en: Extensive research has provided a number of facts about the hazards of alcohol consumption and flying. As little as one bottle of beer can impair flying skills, and the alcohol consumed in these drinks is detectable in the breath and blood for at least 3 hours after drinking. Due to the slow destruction of alcohol, a pilot may still be under the influence 8 hours after drinking a moderate amount of alcohol. Even after the body completely destroys a moderate amount of alcohol, a pilot can still be severely impaired for many hours by a hangover. Always remember, “8 hours from bottle to throttle,” though it is much safer to allow at least 12 to 24 hours between “bottle and throttle.” Answer (B) is incorrect. A consistently high rate of fatal alcohol-related aircraft accidents emphasizes that alcohol and flying are a potentially lethal combination. Answer (C) is incorrect. No amount of alcohol enhances the human system or increases judgment and decision-making abilities.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Alcohol renders a pilot more susceptible to
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Alcohol과 비행은 치명적인 조합이 될 수 있다. 규정은 음주 후 8시간 이내 또는 alcohol 영향 하에서 승무원 임무를 금지하며, alcohol은 disorientation과 hypoxia 감수성도 높인다.
questions.explanation_en: A consistently high rate of fatal alcohol-related aircraft accidents emphasizes that alcohol and flying are a potentially lethal combination. The Federal Aviation Regulations prohibit pilots from performing crewmember duties within 8 hours of drinking any alcoholic beverage or while under the influence of alcohol. Alcohol also renders a pilot much more susceptible to disorientation and hypoxia. Always remember, “8 hours from bottle to throttle,” though it is much safer to allow at least 12 to 24 hours between “bottle and throttle.” Answer (B) is incorrect. Alcohol renders a pilot much more susceptible to disorientation, not indigestion. Answer (C) is incorrect. Alcohol may cause sickness, but it is not known as airsickness. Alcohol renders a pilot much more susceptible to disorientation and hypoxia.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: You attended a party last night and you consumed several glasses of wine. You are planning to fly your aircraft home and have been careful to make sure 8 hours have passed since your last alcoholic drink. You can make the flight now only if you are not under the influence of alcohol and your blood alcohol level is
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 14 CFR Part 91은 음주 후 최소 8시간이 지나야 하고 혈중 alcohol 농도가 0.04% 미만이어야 한다고 요구한다. 둘 중 하나라도 충족하지 못하면 비행할 수 없다.
questions.explanation_en: 14 CFR Part 91 requires that blood alcohol level be less than .04% and that 8 hr. pass between drinking alcohol and piloting an aircraft. A pilot with a blood alcohol level of .04% or greater after 8 hr. cannot fly until the blood alcohol level falls below that amount. Even though blood alcohol may be well below .04%, a pilot cannot fly sooner than 8 hr. after drinking alcohol. Answer (B) is incorrect. The legal limit for motor vehicle operation in many states is .08%. However, to operate an aircraft, a pilot’s blood alcohol level must be below .04%, and 8 hr. must have passed since consuming the last drink. Answer (C) is incorrect. The legal limit to operate an aircraft is .04%. With a blood alcohol level of 0.0%, a pilot would be legal to fly as long as it has been greater than 8 hr. since the last alcoholic beverage.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: While experiencing a hangover, a pilot

choices.text: will have impaired motor and mental responses.
is no longer under the influence of alcohol.
may experience discomfort, but no impairment.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Hangover 상태에서도 운동·인지 반응 저하가 남아 있으므로 조종사는 여전히 alcohol의 영향을 받고 있는 것으로 보아야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: While experiencing a hangover, a pilot is still under the influence of alcohol. Although a pilot may think (s)he is functioning normally, motor and mental response impairment is still present. Answer (B) is incorrect. Considerable amounts of alcohol can remain in the body for over 16 hours, and the effects and symptoms of a hangover are because of the influence of alcohol. Answer (C) is incorrect. Although a pilot may think (s)he is functioning normally, motor and mental response impairment is still present.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Which is a common symptom of hyperventilation?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Hyperventilation은 스트레스 등으로 과도하게 호흡해 CO2를 지나치게 배출하는 상태이다. 어지러움, 질식감, 졸림, 손발 저림, 차가운 느낌 등이 나타날 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Hyperventilation results from an abnormal increase in the volume of air breathed in and out of the lungs. It can occur subconsciously when a stressful situation is encountered. The result is an excessive amount of carbon dioxide removed from the body. The symptoms are lightheadedness, suffocation, drowsiness, tingling of the extremities, and coolness. Answer (B) is incorrect. Hyperventilation distorts one’s abilities; it does not improve them. Answer (C) is incorrect. Decreasing the breathing rate is one way to overcome hyperventilation. It is not a symptom of it.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Which would most likely result in hyperventilation?

choices.text: An extremely slow rate of breathing and insufficient oxygen.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 과호흡은 무의식적으로 호흡량이 과도하게 증가해 체내 CO2가 지나치게 빠져나가는 현상으로, lightheadedness, suffocation, drowsiness, tingling, coolness 등의 증상이 나타난다.
questions.explanation_en: Hyperventilation results from an abnormal increase in the volume of air breathed in and out of the lungs. It can occur subconsciously when a stressful situation is encountered. The result is an excessive amount of carbon dioxide removed from the body. The symptoms are lightheadedness, suffocation, drowsiness, tingling of the extremities, and coolness. Answer (B) is incorrect. Excessive consumption of alcohol would most likely result in hypoxia, not hyperventilation. Answer (C) is incorrect. A slow rate of breathing is the cure for hyperventilation, and insufficient oxygen is the cause of hypoxia, not hyperventilation.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Scanning procedures for effective collision avoidance should constitute

choices.text: looking outside for 15 seconds, then inside for 5 seconds, then repeat.
1 minute inside scanning, then 1 minute outside scanning, then repeat.
looking outside every 30 seconds except in radar contact when outside scanning is unnecessary.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. VFR에서 cockpit 내부 시각작업은 외부 scan 시간의 약 1/4~1/3 이하가 적절하다. 예를 들어 외부를 16초 scan할 때 instrument panel은 약 4~5초 이내로 본다.
questions.explanation_en: Studies show that the amount of time the pilot spends on visual tasks inside the cabin should be no more than one-fourth to one-third of scan time outside, or no more than 4 to 5 seconds on the instrument panel for every 16 seconds of outside scanning when in VFR conditions. Answer (B) is incorrect. Pilots should spend the majority of scan time outside the airplane when in VFR conditions. Answer (C) is incorrect. Pilots should spend the majority of scan time outside the airplane, and outside scanning is necessary when in radar contact in VFR conditions.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: What is the most effective way to use the eyes during night flight?

choices.text: Look only at far away, dim lights.
Scan slowly to permit offcenter viewing.
Concentrate directly on each object for a few seconds.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 야간에는 눈이 중심부보다 약간 벗어난 곳의 물체를 더 잘 감지하므로 천천히 scan하고 off-center viewing을 활용해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Physiologically, the eyes are most effective at seeing objects off center at night. Accordingly, a pilot should scan slowly to permit off-center viewing. Answer (A) is incorrect. Pilots must look at their gauges and instruments, which are about 2 ft. in front of them. Answer (C) is incorrect. Peripheral (off-center) vision is more effective at night.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Which observed target aircraft would be of most concern with respect to collision avoidance?

choices.text: One which appears to be ahead and moving from left to right at high speed.
One which appears to be ahead and moving from right to left at slow speed.
One which appears to be ahead with no lateral or vertical movement and is increasing in size.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 상대운동 없이 한 scan quadrant에 계속 머무는 항공기는 collision course일 가능성이 높다. 좌우·상하 움직임이 없는데 크기만 커지면 즉시 회피해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Any aircraft that appears to have no relative motion and stays in one scan quadrant is likely to be on a collision course. If the target shows no lateral or vertical motion but increases in size, take evasive action. Answer (A) is incorrect. An airplane ahead of you and moving from left to right should pass in front of you. Answer (B) is incorrect. An airplane ahead of you and moving from right to left should pass in front of you.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: When using the Earth’s horizon as a reference point to determine the relative position of other aircraft, most concern would be for aircraft

choices.text: above the horizon and increasing in size.
on the horizon with little relative movement.
on the horizon and increasing in size.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 다른 항공기가 horizon 위면 보통 더 높은 경로, 아래면 더 낮은 경로이다. Horizon 부근에서 상대운동이 거의 없고 크기가 커진다면 같은 고도에서 접근하는 충돌위험이 있을 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Many pilots use the horizon as a reference point to determine the relative altitude of other aircraft. If the aircraft is above the horizon, it is probably on a higher flight path than you. An aircraft that appears to be below the horizon is probably flying at lower altitude. Accordingly, an airplane that appears to be on the horizon and does not show much relative movement may be at your altitude. Any aircraft that appears to increase in size is coming toward you. Answer (A) is incorrect. An airplane above the horizon is probably at a higher altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. An airplane on the horizon without movement may be traveling in the same direction as you.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: A pilot is more subject to spatial disorientation when

choices.text: ignoring or overcoming the sensations of muscles and inner ear.
eyes are moved often in the process of cross-checking the flight instruments.
body sensations are used to interpret flight attitudes.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Spatial disorientation은 여러 감각기관이 뇌에 잘못된 정보를 보내 일시적인 방향·자세 혼란이 생기는 상태이다. 신체감각으로 항공기 자세를 판단할수록 위험이 커진다.
questions.explanation_en: Spatial disorientation is a state of temporary confusion resulting from misleading information being sent to the brain by various sensory organs. Using body sensations to interpret flight attitudes makes pilots more susceptible to spatial disorientation. Answer (A) is incorrect. Ignoring or overcoming the sensations of muscles and inner ear is a means of avoiding (not becoming subject to) spatial disorientation. Answer (B) is incorrect. Rapid eye movements have little or no impact on spatial disorientation, and visual reference to reliable flight instruments helps avoid spatial disorientation.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Which procedure is recommended to prevent or overcome spatial disorientation?

choices.text: Reduce head and eye movement to the greatest possible extent.
Rely entirely on the indications of the flight instruments.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Spatial disorientation을 극복하는 가장 좋은 방법은 신체감각을 믿지 말고 flight instrument와 이용 가능한 ground reference에 전적으로 의존하는 것이다.
questions.explanation_en: The best way to overcome the effects of spatial disorientation is to rely entirely on the airplane’s flight instruments and/or ground references (if available) and not on body sensations. Answer (A) is incorrect. Head and eye movement has little effect on spatial disorientation. Answer (B) is incorrect. Relying on the kinesthetic sense encourages, rather than prevents, spatial disorientation.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: When making an approach to a narrower-than-usual runway, without VASI assistance, the pilot should be aware that the approach

choices.text: altitude may be higher than it appears.
altitude may be lower than it appears.
may result in leveling off too high and landing hard.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 평소보다 좁은 활주로는 실제보다 더 높은 고도에 있는 것처럼 느끼게 해 조종사가 낮은 접근을 하게 만들 수 있으며, 장애물 충돌·short landing 위험이 생긴다.
questions.explanation_en: A narrower-than-usual runway can create the illusion that the aircraft is at a higher altitude than it actually is. A pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach, with the risk of striking objects along the approach path. Answer (A) is incorrect. Wider-than-usual runways, not narrower-than-usual runways, may result in higher-than-desired approaches. Answer (C) is incorrect. Leveling off too high is a result of not recognizing the illusion created by a wider-than-usual runway, not a narrower-than-usual runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: The illusion of being in a nose-up attitude which may occur during a rapid acceleration takeoff is known as
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 이륙 중 급가속은 nose-up한 것 같은 착각을 만들 수 있다. 이를 보정하려고 밀면 실제로 nose-low 또는 dive attitude에 들어갈 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: A rapid acceleration during takeoff can create the illusion of being in a nose-up attitude. The disoriented pilot could push the airplane into a nose-low or dive attitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. The inversion illusion results from an abrupt change from climb to straight-and-level flight, which can create an illusion of tumbling backwards. Answer (B) is incorrect. Autokinesis refers to a static light appearing to move about when stared at for many seconds in the dark.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: While making prolonged constant rate turns under IFR conditions, an abrupt head movement can create the illusion of rotation on an entirely different axis. This is known as
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 장시간 일정률 선회 중 갑자기 머리를 크게 움직이면 Coriolis illusion으로 전혀 다른 축의 회전감을 느낄 수 있다. IFR에서 긴 선회 중에는 갑작스럽고 큰 머리 움직임을 피해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Abrupt head movement in a prolonged constant-rate turn that has ceased stimulating the motion-sensing system can create the illusion of rotation or movement on an entirely different axis. This is known as the Coriolis illusion. The disoriented pilot could maneuver the aircraft in a dangerous attitude in an attempt to stop rotation. This effect may be prevented by not making sudden, extreme head movements, particularly while making prolonged constant-rate turns under IFR conditions. Answer (A) is incorrect. Autokinesis refers to a static light appearing to move about when stared at for many seconds in the dark. Answer (C) is incorrect. The term “leans” refers to an abrupt correction of a banked attitude that has been entered too slowly to stimulate the motion-sensing system in the inner ear and can create the illusion of bank in the opposite direction.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: In the dark, a stationary light will appear to move when stared at for a period of time. This illusion is known as
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 어두운 곳에서 고정된 불빛을 오래 바라보면 움직이는 것처럼 보이는 autokinesis가 생길 수 있으며, 그 불빛에 항공기를 맞추려다 자세를 잃을 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: In the dark, a static, or stationary, light will appear to move about when stared at for many seconds. The disoriented pilot may lose control of the aircraft in attempting to align it with the light. Answer (A) is incorrect. Somatogravic illusion occurs with a rapid acceleration during takeoff, creating the illusion of being in a nose-up attitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. A ground lighting illusion refers to lights on a straight path such as a road being mistaken by a pilot for runway or approach lights.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: When making a landing over darkened or featureless terrain such as water or snow, a pilot should be aware of the possibility of illusion. The approach may appear to be too
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 물·어두운 지형·눈 덮인 featureless terrain처럼 지상 특징이 없으면 실제보다 높게 느껴져 필요 이상으로 낮은 접근을 할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The absence of ground features as when landing over water, darkened areas, and terrain made featureless by snow can create the illusion that the airplane is at a higher altitude than it actually is. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower-than-appropriate approach. Answer (B) is incorrect. The illusion is that the aircraft is at a higher altitude than it is, not too low. Answer (C) is incorrect. The illusion is that the aircraft is at a higher altitude than it is, not too shallow.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Haze can give the illusion that the aircraft is

choices.text: closer to the runway than it actually is.
farther from the runway than it actually is.
the same distance from the runway as when there is no restriction to visibility.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Atmospheric haze는 활주로가 실제보다 더 멀리 있는 것처럼 보이게 해 조종사가 낮은 접근을 하도록 만들 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Atmospheric haze can create the illusion of being at a greater distance from the runway. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach. Answer (A) is incorrect. Bright runway and approach lights or a wider-than-usual runway, not haze, can give the illusion of being closer to the runway. Answer (C) is incorrect. Haze can give the illusion of being farther, not the same distance, from the runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Sudden penetration of fog can create the illusion of
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fog 안으로 진입하면 pitch-up한 것처럼 느끼는 착각이 생길 수 있고, 이를 잘못 보정하면 접근각을 갑자기 가파르게 만들 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Penetration of fog can create the illusion of pitching up. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will steepen the approach, often quite abruptly. Answer (B) is incorrect. Sudden penetration of fog can create the illusion of pitching up, not down. Answer (C) is incorrect. Sudden penetration of fog can create the illusion of pitching up, not leveling off.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Penetrating fog while flying an approach at night, you might experience the illusion of
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 빛의 굴절(refractory effects)은 nose-high attitude로 느끼게 하는 시각착각을 만들 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Refractory effects can cause the perception of a nose high attitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. This results from the illusion of being farther away from the runway; thus, the pilot responds by flying a lower approach. Answer (C) is incorrect. This illusion is primarily perceived during and after motion disturbances leading to spatial disorientation.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: The illusion associated with landing on a narrower than usual runway may result in the pilot flying a

choices.text: lower approach with the risk of striking objects along the approach path or landing short.
slower approach with the risk of reducing airspeed below VSO or landing hard.
higher approach with the risk of leveling out high and landing hard or overshooting the runway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 좁은 활주로는 실제보다 높은 고도에 있는 것처럼 느끼게 하므로 접근을 지나치게 낮게 해 장애물 충돌이나 runway short landing을 유발할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: A narrower-than-usual runway can create an illusion that the aircraft is at a higher altitude than it actually is, which could result in striking objects along the flight path or landing short. Answer (B) is incorrect. Runway width has no effect on the perceived speed in an approach to landing. Answer (C) is incorrect. A wider-, not narrower-, than-usual runway can create the illusion that the aircraft is lower than actual altitude, creating the risk of the pilot leveling out the aircraft high and landing hard or overshooting the runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: What illusion, if any, can rain on the windscreen create?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Windshield의 rain은 실제보다 runway 위에서 더 높게 있는 것처럼 보이게 해 조종사가 낮은 접근을 하도록 만들 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Rain on the windscreen can create the illusion of greater height above the runway. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach. Answer (A) is incorrect. Rain on the windscreen can create the illusion of being higher than actual. Answer (B) is incorrect. Rain on the windscreen can create the illusion of being higher, not lower, than actual.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: You have just touched down hard on a narrower than usual runway at night. You realize you just experienced
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Hard landing은 늦은 flare와 연관될 수 있으며, 좁은 활주로가 실제보다 높게 느끼게 하는 runway-width illusion이 원인이 될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: A hard landing implies a late flare, which can be caused by runway width illusion. A narrower-than-usual runway can create the illusion that the airplane is at a higher-than-actual altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. There is no defined runway elevation illusion; however, the runway width illusion can give a pilot the impression (s)he is at a higher altitude than (s)he really is, leading to a hard landing due to a late flare for landing. Answer (C) is incorrect. The featureless terrain illusion assumes the runway is not in proximity to any visible ground features. This illusion can result from overwater landings, snow covered landscapes, or dark ground. A hard landing on a narrow runway implies the pilot suffered from the runway width illusion, not a featureless terrain illusion.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Staring at static light in the darkness can create the illusion of

choices.text: autokinesis which could lead to loss of control.
halo vision and night vision loss.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Autokinesis는 어두운 곳의 정지된 불빛을 몇 초 이상 응시하면 움직이는 것처럼 보이는 현상이다.
questions.explanation_en: Autokinesis occurs when a static, or stationary, light in the dark appears to move about when stared at for many seconds. The disoriented pilot will lose control of the aircraft in attempting to align it with the light. Answer (A) is incorrect. Autonomic involuntary muscle response can happen day or night. It is controlled by the nervous system. Answer (C) is incorrect. Halos are bright circles that appear to surround a source of light, such as oncoming car headlights. Night vision loss is from white lights shining in the eyes. Autokinesis happens with even dim lights and does not cause night vision loss.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: You just touched down faster than planned in haze on a runway at night. You realize you have just experienced
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Haze는 runway가 더 멀리 있는 것처럼 느끼게 해 낮은 접근을 만들고, 정상보다 빠른 속도로 갑자기 touchdown할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Atmospheric haze can create the illusion of being at a greater distance from the runway. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach, abruptly touching down at a faster than normal landing speed. Answer (B) is incorrect. Runway width illusion is created by a narrower-than-usual runway. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach and risk striking objects along the approach path or landing short. Answer (C) is incorrect. An absence of ground features can create the illusion that the aircraft is at a higher altitude than it actually is. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach and a hard, short landing.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: You just touched down hard in the rain on a narrower than usual runway at night. You have just experienced
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Windshield rain과 narrow-runway illusion은 모두 실제보다 높게 느끼게 하므로 조종사가 낮은 접근을 해 hard landing으로 이어질 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Rain in the windscreen can create the illusion of greater height. Runway width illusion (narrower-than-usual runway) can create the illusion that the aircraft is at a higher altitude than it actually is. The pilot who does not recognize these two together will fly a lower approach that results in a hard landing. Answer (A) is incorrect. Ground lighting illusion is caused by lights along a straight path such as a road, and even lights on moving trains can be mistaken for runway and approach lights. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a higher than normal approach, landing long. Answer (B) is incorrect. Runway length illusion with a runway that is short will cause the pilot who does not recognize this illusion to fly a higher than normal approach. A runway that is longer will cause just the opposite. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Human behavior

choices.text: rarely results in accidents unless deliberate actions are performed.
causes three out of four accidents.
is well understood, so behavioral induced accidents are exceedingly rare occurrences.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Human behavior 연구는 사람이 왜 특정 방식으로 행동하는지 이해해 항공 human error의 결과를 줄이는 데 사용된다. 오류 자체를 완전히 제거할 수는 없으므로 예측 가능한 오류를 훈련과 시스템으로 관리하는 것이 핵심이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The study of human behavior is an attempt to explain how and why humans function the way they do. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) utilizes studies of human behavior in an attempt to reduce human error in aviation. Three out of four accidents result from human error. Eliminating human error is an unrealistic goal since errors are a normal part of human behavior. On the other hand, realizing that many aviation accidents are preventable means designing ways to reduce the consequences of human error.
